Here ist some context: Prompt:

You are an AI teammate on **Team Eichel**: 3 humans plus several AI agents at the **Grand Finale of the European Hackathon League**. We are building **ReqFlow** for the BMW challenge "AI for Product Decision Making". It is a **native desktop app (Electron: Windows, macOS, Linux), not a web app**. An n8n-style workflow turns customer feedback, BMW data and web research into prioritized, evidence-linked car requirements. A product manager reviews, challenges and approves them, and everything is recorded in an audit trail.  **Your workstream:** WS<N> — <name> (see docs/WORKSTREAMS.md). If none is given, read docs/STATUS.md, claim the first `open` workstream that fits your strengths, and tell the human which one you took.  ## Start (first 10 minutes) 1. The code lives in https://github.com/EHL-Team-Eichel/reqflow. Clone it, or `git pull` if you already    have it. Work in this repo and don't create new ones. 2. Read in this order: AGENTS.md → docs/STATUS.md → PRODUCT.md → docs/ARCHITECTURE.md → your section of    docs/WORKSTREAMS.md. 3. Run `npm install`. Then run `entire status`. If Entire isn't enabled for your tool, run    `entire enable --agent <claude-code|codex|opencode|antigravity>` and commit what it adds. 4. Run `git switch -c ws<N>-<slug>`, or continue the branch listed in docs/STATUS.md. 5. Claim the workstream: set your section in docs/STATUS.md to `in progress`, then commit and push.  ## How we work - **Stay in your lane.** Edit only the paths your workstream owns. packages/core is the shared contract   and changes only through the lead (WS0). Put requests in your section of docs/STATUS.md. - **Commit small, push immediately.** Commit every working step. Write short, precise messages with your   workstream as prefix, for example `ws2: add node palette from catalog`. - **Integrate often.** Run `git pull --rebase origin main` at least hourly. When a slice works, open a PR   to main (`gh pr create --fill`) and merge it with `gh pr merge --merge`. Don't squash, so Entire's   checkpoint trailers survive. Never force-push main. - **Prove it.** Run `npm run check` before merging. For UI work, also run `npm run smoke` and look at the   screenshots in apps/desktop/out/smoke/. Never claim something works without that evidence. - **Use every tool you have.** Check which agent CLIs are installed (claude, codex, opencode, agy).   Delegate bulky, well-specified work to them (scaffolding, tests, research digests) and run it in   parallel. You stay responsible: review the diff and rerun the checks yourself. - **Aim for the demo.** Optimize for the judging criteria in AGENTS.md: trustworthy sources, transparent   reasoning, explainable prioritization, honest uncertainty, and the PM in control.  ## Hard rules - **The repo and Entire's session transcripts are public.** Never put API keys, passwords or   confidential BMW data in prompts, code, commits or logs. BMW files stay in data/raw/, which is   gitignored. - **The AI never decides.** Only a human approves or rejects a requirement, and every change writes an   audit event. - **Never invent** sources, evidence or test results. Don't present stubs as finished. - **Ask the humans only** about product direction, credentials, or anything public or irreversible.   Otherwise decide, note the decision in your docs/STATUS.md section, and keep going.  ## Handoff The next agent starts from docs/STATUS.md. Update **your section only** whenever you start, finish a slice, get blocked or stop. Include the status, the branch, what works and how to verify it, what's next, and any open questions. If the product itself changes, update PRODUCT.md too.  You remain part of the hackathon until a human tells you it has concluded. When your workstream is done, take the next `open` item in docs/STATUS.md, or ask the humans what would help the demo most. 1: # AGENTS.md — read this first
2: 
3: ## What we're building
4: 
5: **ReqFlow** is a hackathon prototype for the BMW challenge _"AI for Product Decision Making"_: a
6: **native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron, not a web app) with three tabs. On
7: **Data Flow**, an n8n-style flow of **building blocks** (Custom, Raw, Research, AI Filter, AI Splitter,
8: HIL, Add to Car; some expand into their own inner workplace) turns customer and market data into
9: prioritized, evidence-linked car requirements. The **Car** tab shows them for the PM to review, and
10: **Settings** configures the app, global parameters and collaboration. Full spec: [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md). Your task: [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md).
11: Current state and handoffs: [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).
12: 
13: ## The challenge in brief (from `context/`)
14: 
15: - **Goal:** help BMW product managers define, justify and prioritize **customer-facing requirements
16:   for the successor** of an existing vehicle, thinking **3–5 years ahead**. The PM stays in control of
17:   every decision.
18: - **Vehicles and markets:** the 1, 5 or 7 Series, in Europe, China or the US. Demo **one derivative in one
19:   market** (ours: 5 Series Sedan, EU), but don't build a one-off.
20: - **BMW provides, per vehicle:** customer feedback, equipment data, sales volumes and a customer study.
21:   We may add web sources such as competitors, reviews and market or technology trends.
22: - **The app must:** ingest the data and enrich it from the web → extract signals (complaints, unmet needs,
23:   competitor advantages, trends), **each linked to its sources** → derive clear, actionable, realistic
24:   requirements → prioritize them with explainable logic → let the PM approve, reject, edit or challenge
25:   them → record everything in an **audit trail** (who or what, when, and why).
26: - **Each requirement needs:** a unique ID, an actionable description, linked findings and sources, a
27:   priority or score, the prioritization rationale, an evidence level, assumptions and uncertainties, and
28:   a decision status.
29: - **In scope:** features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment and digital services,
30:   design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging as the customer experiences them,
31:   and variants and packages. **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, engineering specs, and
32:   pricing or business cases (rough effort may be used as a priority factor).
33: - **Judges value:** trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning, thoughtful prioritization, honest
34:   handling of uncertainty and **conflicting evidence**, and focus on customer value. Depth in one area
35:   beats shallow coverage of everything.
36: - **BMW process we mirror:** situation analysis → structure and context (classify, cluster, dedupe) →
37:   requirements definition (measurable targets and acceptance criteria) → prioritization (customer and
38:   business) → documentation and tracking. _"From 1 billion findings to 1,000 requirements to one car."_
39: 
40: ## Rules for every agent
41: 
42: 1. **Stay in your lane.** Edit only the paths your workstream owns (see WORKSTREAMS.md). Do you need
43:    something changed elsewhere? Write it in your final report instead of editing it yourself.
44: 2. **`packages/core` is the contract.** Build against it and don't change it on your own. If you need a
45:    contract change, propose it in your final report. The lead merges contract changes.
46: 3. **No real data in git.** BMW files go in `data/raw/` (gitignored). Use synthetic fixtures from
47:    `@reqflow/core/fixtures` until the real data arrives. Never commit or print API keys.
48: 4. **No silent failures.** Validate inputs with the Zod schemas, throw clear errors, and never invent
49:    sources or evidence. Every finding needs a verbatim excerpt.
50: 5. **AI never decides.** Only a human sets `approved`, `rejected` or `deferred`. Every change to a
51:    requirement writes an AuditEvent.
52: 6. **Prove it works.** Add colocated `*.test.ts` files. Before you report done, run
53:    `npm run typecheck && npm test` from the repo root. For UI work, also run `npm run smoke` and look at
54:    the screenshots in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`.
55: 7. **Respect the process split.** UI code (renderer) has no Node, no `fs` and no network. It talks to the
56:    main process only through `api` from `@/lib/api` (contract: `packages/core/src/ipc.ts`). Data, AI
57:    calls, files and API keys live in the main process. Build paths with `node:path` so they work on Windows.
58: 8. **Sessions are tracked with [Entire](https://github.com/entireio/cli).** Commit with plain `git`.
59:    Entire attaches your session to each commit as a checkpoint and pushes it on `git push`. Don't
60:    remove its hooks (`.claude/settings.json`, `.git/hooks`) and never put secrets in prompts.
61: 
62: 9. **Hand off in [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).** Claim your workstream there when you start; your
63:    tasks are the checklist in its section, in priority order. Update your own section (and only that
64:    one) when you finish a slice, get blocked or stop: tick done tasks, add a log entry. The next agent
65:    starts from it. The repo and Entire transcripts are **public**, so never paste keys or BMW data anywhere.
66: 
67: ## Commands (repo root, Node ≥ 22.13; works on Windows, macOS, Linux)
68: 
69: ```
70: npm install          # once
71: npm run dev          # opens the desktop app with hot reload
72: npm run smoke        # builds, screenshots every screen, checks the IPC bridge
73: npm test             # vitest, all packages
74: npm run typecheck    # all workspaces
75: npm run format       # prettier
76: npm run package      # installer for your OS → apps/desktop/release/
77: ```
</content>

1: # ReqFlow — product definition
2: 
3: > Working name. One page, the source of truth for **what** we build. **How** is in
4: > [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), **who builds what** in [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md).
5: 
6: ## Problem
7: 
8: Defining the next generation of a BMW vehicle means working out what customers will value 3–5 years
9: from now. Today product managers do this by hand: they read customer feedback, BMW equipment and
10: sales data, customer studies and competitor and market information, then turn it into requirements.
11: It is slow, inconsistent and hard to trace. Months later nobody can say why a requirement exists,
12: what evidence backs it, or who decided it.
13: 
14: ## Product in one sentence
15: 
16: A visual, n8n-style **data flow** built from **building blocks** turns raw customer and market data into
17: **evidence-linked, prioritized car requirements**. A product manager reviews, challenges and decides on
18: them on the **Car** page, and every step is recorded in an **audit trail**.
19: 
20: > Customer requirement = customer-relevant attribute of a car. (BMW briefing)
21: 
22: ## Users
23: 
24: - **Product Manager (primary).** Owns the requirement set for one vehicle line × market. Makes every decision.
25: - **Analyst / PM ops (secondary).** Builds and tunes workflows, connects data and adjusts scoring in Settings.
26: 
27: ## The app — three tabs
28: 
29: A **native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux**, not a web app. Everything runs locally on
30: the PM's machine. BMW files are imported through the system file dialog, results are exported
31: through the save dialog, and API keys are stored in the OS keychain. Only the AI and web-research
32: calls leave the machine. Layout (sketch: `context/Building_Blocks.jpeg`): the page fills the window, and
33: a tab bar at the bottom switches between **Data Flow · Car · Settings** (⌘/Ctrl + 1–3).
34: 
35: | Tab           | What the user does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
36: | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
37: | **Data Flow** | **Building Blocks** on the left, the **Workplace** on the right. Drag blocks (or click them) onto the workplace, connect an output to an input, and set each block's parameters in the inspector. Custom, Research and AI Filter blocks **expand** into their own inner workplace, built from the same blocks. Later: run the flow, see each block's status, counts and logs, and inspect what it produced. A run **pauses at HIL blocks** until a person has reviewed.                                                                                                            |
38: | **Car**       | The output: what the next car should offer. Today a placeholder (a car and the global vehicle/market). WS3 builds the requirement list here. Each requirement has an ID, title, description, measurable targets, category, score breakdown, priority with rationale, evidence level, assumptions, uncertainties, conflicting evidence and status, with a drill-down requirement → findings → verbatim evidence → source, **approve / reject / defer / edit / challenge** (rationale required) and the **audit trail**: who or what changed what, when, from what to what, and why. |
39: | **Settings**  | **App** (theme, workplace grid and minimap, delete confirmation) · **Global parameters** (vehicle line, derivative, code, market, horizon; prioritization weights and thresholds with a live example; output language) · **AI & research** (provider, models, temperature, web research, domains, API-key status) · **Collaboration** (your name and role for the audit trail, team members and invitations, sharing via a shared folder or Git repo, notifications, four-eyes approval) · **About**.                                                                              |
40: 
41: ## The building blocks
42: 
43: | Block           | What it does                                                                                        | Ports              | Inner workplace |
44: | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | --------------- |
45: | **Custom**      | An empty block. Build any sub-flow inside it.                                                       | 1 in · 1 out       | yes             |
46: | **Raw**         | Brings in an Excel file or a database table as one unified data stream.                             | 1 out              | no              |
47: | **Research**    | Searches the web; emits a data stream in the same format as Raw.                                    | 1 out              | yes             |
48: | **AI Filter**   | Keeps the items that match a criterion written in plain language.                                   | 1 in · 1 out       | yes             |
49: | **AI Splitter** | Sorts every item into one branch (e.g. by priority or category). One output per branch.             | 1 in · n out       | no              |
50: | **HIL**         | Human in the loop (capacitor icon): the flow waits until a person has reviewed what passes through. | 1 in · 1 out       | no              |
51: | **Add to Car**  | Adds what arrives to the car's requirements. The input it arrives on sets the ranking.              | one in per ranking | no              |
52: 
53: Parameters are placeholders until each block is built (see `docs/WORKSTREAMS.md`). Spec and ports: `packages/core/src/blocks.ts`.
54: 
55: ## Default flow (template)
56: 
57: The default template mirrors the BMW process slide (`context/` image). The robot icon means the AI does the step on its own; the person icon means a human is involved.
58: 
59: ```
60: Situation analysis        Structure & context          Prioritization                  Review          Documentation
61: ──────────────────        ───────────────────          ──────────────                  ──────          ─────────────
62: Raw: customer feedback ┐
63: Raw: customer study    ┤
64: Raw: equipment data    ┼─▶ AI Filter ───────────────▶ AI Splitter ──must───▶ 🧑 HIL ──┐
65: Raw: sales volumes     ┤   "customer-facing only"     "by priority" ──should─▶ 🧑 HIL ──┼─▶ Add to Car
66: Research: web          ┘   (findings + evidence;       (explainable ──could─────────────┘   (requirements,
67:                             drops regulatory,           weighted       (unreviewed)          ranked by input)
68:                             engineering, pricing)       score)
69: ```
70: 
71: **Where AI acts on its own:** ingestion (Raw, Research), filtering and extracting evidence-linked
72: findings (AI Filter), scoring and routing (AI Splitter), drafting requirements (Add to Car).
73: **Where a human must act:** at every HIL block, and when approving, rejecting, deferring or editing a
74: requirement, overriding a priority or answering a challenge on the Car tab. The AI can **never** set
75: a requirement to `approved` or `rejected`.
76: 
77: ## Core objects (full schemas in `packages/core`)
78: 
79: - **Source** — a dataset, document or web page, with a reliability rating.
80: - **SourceRecord** — one comment, row or paragraph from a source.
81: - **Finding** — a normalized signal (`complaint`, `unmet_need`, `praise`, `competitor_advantage`,
82:   `market_trend` or `usage_pattern`). It always cites ≥ 1 verbatim evidence excerpt.
83: - **Theme** — a cluster of duplicate or related findings.
84: - **Requirement** — `REQ-<vehicle>-<market>-<nnn>`. Holds the description, targets, linked findings and
85:   sources, score, priority with rationale, **evidence level A–D**, assumptions, uncertainties,
86:   conflicting findings and **status** (`proposed → in_review → approved | rejected | deferred`, plus
87:   `challenged`).
88: - **AuditEvent** — actor, action, entity, before/after changes, rationale and timestamp. Never edited or deleted.
89: 
90: ## Prioritization logic (explainable by design)
91: 
92: Six factors, each scored 0–5 with a one-line justification. On every factor, higher means "more worth doing":
93: customer impact · evidence strength · competitive gap · trend momentum (3–5 yr) · brand fit ·
94: ease (the inverse of rough effort/cost).
95: 
96: `score = 100 × Σ(weight × value) / (5 × Σ weight)`. The score maps to **must / should / could / won't**
97: using the thresholds set in Settings. The PM can override the priority, and the override is audited.
98: Evidence level is shown **next to** the score, never hidden inside it. A high score built on
99: D-level (assumption) evidence should catch the eye.
100: 
101: ## Evidence levels
102: 
103: **A** — several independent sources including quantitative BMW data · **B** — several sources, mostly
104: qualitative · **C** — a single source or anecdotal · **D** — rests mainly on forward-looking assumptions.
105: 
106: ## Scope rules (from the briefing)
107: 
108: - **In scope:** customer-facing attributes such as features, equipment, comfort, space, usability,
109:   infotainment and digital services, design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging
110:   _as the customer experiences them_, and variants and packages.
111: - **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, technical and engineering specs, and
112:   pricing or business cases. An AI Filter removes these, and every exclusion is logged with a reason.
113: 
114: ## Demo scenario
115: 
116: **BMW 5 Series Sedan · EU · 5-year horizon.** This is our default. Confirm it once BMW's datasets arrive.
117: 
118: 1. Open the default template, attach the BMW files to the Raw blocks, enable web research, and run.
119: 2. Watch the blocks fill up, then click the AI Filter to see findings with their evidence.
120: 3. The run pauses at the HIL block. On the Car tab, open a must-have and trace it down to a verbatim customer quote.
121: 4. Challenge one requirement. The AI answers. Edit one, approve one with a priority override, and reject one.
122: 5. Resume the run, which publishes and exports. The audit trail shows the full history of one requirement.
123: 6. Switch the scope to another series or market in Settings to show the workflow isn't a one-off.
124: 
125: ## Deliverables checklist (briefing → where we show it)
126: 
127: - [ ] Concept and working prototype → the app and this document
128: - [ ] Structured sample list of requirements with all the required fields → Car tab and export
129: - [ ] End-to-end workflow showing which steps the AI does alone and where a human must act → Data Flow tab (HIL blocks) and the diagram above
130: - [ ] Audit trail from source to decision → audit trail on the Car tab and the requirement History
131: 
132: ## Non-goals for the hackathon
133: 
134: Authentication, live multi-user editing and a sync server (Settings → Collaboration keeps the team and
135: the sharing choice on this computer; sending invitations and syncing come later, if at all), web and
136: mobile versions, signed installers and auto-update. Any of these can be mocked if the
137: demo needs them.

1: # Architecture
2: 
3: ReqFlow is a **native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron), not a web app.
4: Background and alternatives: [decisions/0002-electron-desktop-app.md](decisions/0002-electron-desktop-app.md).
5: Why the flow is built from blocks: [decisions/0003-building-blocks.md](decisions/0003-building-blocks.md).
6: 
7: ## Stack
8: 
9: | Concern         | Choice                                                                                | Why                                                                 |
10: | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
11: | Language        | TypeScript everywhere (npm workspaces)                                                | One shared contract for UI, engine and blocks                       |
12: | App shell       | Electron 44 (pinned, Node 24 inside), electron-vite 5, electron-builder               | Same Chromium on every OS; Node in the main process runs the engine |
13: | UI              | React 19 + React Router (hash routing) + Tailwind 4 + zustand 5                       | Renders from `file://` in the installed app; small, testable stores |
14: | Workflow canvas | `@xyflow/react` (React Flow 12)                                                       | The standard n8n-style node editor                                  |
15: | Schemas         | Zod 4                                                                                 | Runtime validation and TS types from one source                     |
16: | LLM             | Claude API (`@anthropic-ai/sdk`) behind `LlmClient`, plus a `mock` provider           | Swappable; works offline and in tests                               |
17: | Persistence     | SQLite via built-in `node:sqlite`, in the OS app-data folder                          | Zero setup, no native module to rebuild per OS                      |
18: | Tests           | Vitest (colocated `*.test.ts`) + `npm run smoke` (clicks through the app in Electron) | Fast unit tests; a real-app check without clicking                  |
19: 
20: ## Repo layout
21: 
22: ```
23: .
24: ├── AGENTS.md  PRODUCT.md  README.md   ← start here
25: ├── context/                           ← original hackathon briefing + the app sketch (read-only)
26: ├── docs/                              ← ARCHITECTURE, WORKSTREAMS, STATUS, decisions/ (ADRs)
27: ├── data/
28: │   ├── raw/        (gitignored)       ← BMW-provided datasets
29: │   └── samples/                       ← small synthetic datasets for dev
30: ├── packages/
31: │   ├── core/       ← CONTRACT: domain schemas, blocks.ts (block specs), graph.ts (graph rules), IPC API, fixtures
32: │   ├── engine/     ← block contract + registry (done); executor (WS1)
33: │   ├── blocks/     ← block implementations, one folder per block + default template
34: │   ├── llm/        ← LlmClient implementations: anthropic, mock (WS7)
35: │   └── db/         ← SQLite repositories, AuditLogger, FileStore (WS1)
36: └── apps/desktop/                      ← the Electron app
37:     ├── electron.vite.config.ts  electron-builder.yml  build/ (icons)
38:     └── src/
39:         ├── main/       ← Node: window, IPC handlers, wiring of engine/db/llm, smoke test
40:         ├── preload/    ← the bridge: allow-listed invoke + run-update events (keep tiny)
41:         └── renderer/src/
42:             ├── pages/        DataflowPage · CarPage · SettingsPage
43:             ├── components/   dataflow/ (editor + its store) · settings/ · shell/ (bottom tabs) · ui/ (shared controls)
44:             ├── lib/          api.ts (the only way to main) · settings.ts (settings store) · theme.ts
45:             └── router.tsx  globals.css (design tokens, light + dark)
46: ```
47: 
48: Dependency direction (no cycles): `core ← engine ← blocks`, `core ← llm`, `core ← db`, and
49: `apps/desktop/src/main` → all of them. The renderer imports only `@reqflow/core` (types, block specs,
50: graph rules, fixtures). It never imports engine, db, llm or blocks.
51: 
52: ## Processes and security
53: 
54: ```
55: renderer (React, sandboxed)  ──api.x.y(…)──▶  preload (allow-list)  ──IPC──▶  main (Node)
56:    no Node, no fs, no network                                              engine · SQLite · LLM · files · keychain
57:            ◀──────────────── runs.onUpdate(run) push events ────────────────────────┘
58: ```
59: 
60: - `contextIsolation`, `sandbox` and no `nodeIntegration`. Production builds get a strict CSP
61:   (`connect-src 'self'`): all network calls (Claude, web search) happen in main.
62: - The preload only forwards channels listed in `IPC_INVOKE_METHODS`. Main also checks that the sender is the app window.
63: - The window never navigates away. `http(s)` links open in the user's browser.
64: - API keys are entered in Settings, encrypted with Electron `safeStorage` (OS keychain) and never sent to
65:   the renderer. In dev, `apps/desktop/.env` is also read (see `.env.example`).
66: 
67: ## The building blocks (`packages/core/src/blocks.ts`)
68: 
69: A workflow is a tree of **workplaces**. Each workplace holds blocks and edges. Seven kinds of block
70: are in the palette, defined once in `BLOCK_SPECS` (label, description, group, params, ports, whether
71: it has an inner workplace):
72: 
73: | Block       | Ports                                 | Inner workplace | Params (placeholders for now)                 |
74: | ----------- | ------------------------------------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
75: | Custom      | 1 in · 1 out                          | yes             | none                                          |
76: | Raw         | no input · 1 out (data stream)        | no              | Excel upload or database, dataset, file/query |
77: | Research    | no input · 1 out (same format as Raw) | yes             | question, source types, market, age, results  |
78: | AI Filter   | 1 in · 1 out (kept)                   | yes             | criterion, model, min. confidence             |
79: | AI Splitter | 1 in · one out **per branch**         | no              | split by, branches (list → ports), model      |
80: | HIL         | 1 in · 1 out                          | no              | reviewer, instructions, approvals, edits      |
81: | Add to Car  | one in **per ranking** · no output    | no              | rankings (list → ports), vehicle, market      |
82: 
83: - **Ports** come from `blockPorts(block)`. They can depend on params (the splitter's `branches`, Add to
84:   Car's `rankings`), and port ids are positional (`out-0`, `in-2`). When params change, `setBlockParams`
85:   removes edges on ports that no longer exist and returns them, so the editor can tell the user.
86: - **Params** are declared as `ParamSpec`s (text, textarea, number, slider, select, multiselect, toggle,
87:   list, file). The editor renders a form from them, and `parseBlockParams` validates strictly (unknown
88:   keys and wrong types are errors). Select options with the value `"global"` mean "use Settings →
89:   Global parameters".
90: - **Inner workplaces** (Custom, Research, AI Filter) hold a sub-flow built from the same blocks,
91:   recursively. Each one has fixed **boundary blocks**: one `block_input` per input port of the parent
92:   and one `block_output` per output port. They are created with the block and can't be deleted.
93: - **Ids** are unique across the whole tree, so run status and outputs are keyed by block id alone.
94: - **Graph rules** live in `packages/core/src/graph.ts` and are shared by the editor and the engine:
95:   `checkConnection` (ports exist, no self-loop, no duplicates, no cycles), `connect`, `removeBlocks`,
96:   `setBlockParams`, `graphAt` / `updateGraphAt` (navigate the tree), `validateGraph` (everything,
97:   recursively). Several edges may enter one input (merged) or leave one output (fan-out).
98: 
99: ## Data flow: one envelope per port
100: 
101: Every port carries a `PipelineData` envelope (`sources, records, findings, themes, requirements`).
102: Raw and Research emit sources and records (the "unified data stream"). Later blocks enrich the same
103: envelope: AI Filter keeps matching items (and extracts evidence-linked findings), AI Splitter routes
104: items to one branch each, HIL passes on what the reviewer approved, and Add to Car turns what arrives
105: into requirements; the input it arrives on sets the ranking. Several edges into one input are combined
106: with `mergePipelineData` (concatenate, de-duplicate by `id`, later edge wins).
107: 
108: ```ts
109: defineBlock({
110:   kind: "ai_filter",
111:   async run(inputs, params, ctx) {
112:     const input = inputs.in; // one envelope per input port id
113:     /* ctx.llm, ctx.audit, ctx.log … */
114:     return { status: "ok", outputs: { out: kept } }; // one envelope per output port id
115:   },
116: });
117: ```
118: 
119: ## Engine semantics (WS1 implements, everyone relies on)
120: 
121: 1. **Validate before running** with `validateGraph`, and check that every block kind (except
122:    Custom) has an implementation (`BlockRegistry.missing()`). If anything fails, the run fails before it
123:    starts, with per-block errors.
124: 2. **Execute each workplace in topological order.** A block's input per port is the merge of what its
125:    incoming edges carry. Store each block's output per port and push `BlockRun` status, counts, logs
126:    and progress via `runs.onUpdate`.
127: 3. **Inner workplaces.** A block whose inner workplace contains blocks runs that sub-flow: each
128:    `block_input` emits what arrived on its parent port, and what reaches each `block_output` becomes
129:    the parent's output on that port. A Custom block always runs its sub-flow. Research and AI Filter run
130:    their built-in implementation while their inner workplace is empty.
131: 4. **Failure.** A block that throws is marked `failed`, its downstream blocks `skipped`, and the run
132:    `failed`. Nothing is partially published.
133: 5. **Pause / resume.** HIL returns `{ status: "paused" }` → the run is `waiting_for_review`.
134:    `runs.resume` reloads what the reviewer changed, re-invokes the block with `ctx.resumed = true`, and continues.
135: 6. **Cancel.** The run's `AbortSignal` fires, and blocks must stop promptly.
136: 7. **Audit.** The engine logs `run.*` events, blocks log what they create or change, and handlers log human actions.
137: 
138: ## IPC API (`packages/core/src/ipc.ts`)
139: 
140: UI code calls `api.<namespace>.<method>(…)` from `@/lib/api`. Main implements `ReqflowHandlers`
141: (`apps/desktop/src/main/handlers.ts`). Failures arrive as `ReqflowError` with a `code`
142: (`invalid_input`, `not_found`, `not_implemented`, `internal`, …). Arguments must be plain data. Main
143: validates every argument with the Zod schemas, because the renderer counts as untrusted input.
144: 
145: | Method                                               | Purpose                                                                                                                             |
146: | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
147: | `app.info()`                                         | Version, OS, data directory (**built**)                                                                                             |
148: | `templates.list()`                                   | Workflow templates (`BMW_DEFAULT_TEMPLATE`) (**built**)                                                                             |
149: | `workflows.list/get/save/remove`                     | Workflow CRUD. `save` assigns the id and bumps `version`                                                                            |
150: | `files.import()`                                     | Native open dialog → copies the file into the data dir → `StoredFileInfo` (`null` if cancelled). Raw's `file` param stores it       |
151: | `runs.start/get/list/blockOutput/resume/cancel`      | Run lifecycle. `blockOutput` returns that block's output per port                                                                   |
152: | `runs.onUpdate(listener)`                            | Push events on every status, progress or log change (no polling)                                                                    |
153: | `requirements.list(filter)` · `requirements.get(id)` | Latest versions · `RequirementDetail` (findings, evidence, sources, versions)                                                       |
154: | `requirements.edit(id, RequirementEdit)`             | PM edit, rationale required → new version and audit                                                                                 |
155: | `requirements.decide(id, RequirementDecision)`       | Approve / reject / defer / challenge / reopen. A challenge makes the AI answer (`challenge_answered`) and returns it to `in_review` |
156: | `audit.list(filter)`                                 | Audit events, ascending by time                                                                                                     |
157: | `settings.get/save` · `settings.secrets/setSecret`   | `Settings` (save logs `settings.changed` with a diff) · API-key status / store a key in the keychain                                |
158: | `exports.requirements({ runId, format })`            | Native save dialog → JSON / CSV / Markdown (logs `export.created`)                                                                  |
159: 
160: To add a method: add it to `ReqflowApi` **and** `IPC_INVOKE_METHODS` (the compiler enforces both),
161: then implement it in `handlers.ts`.
162: 
163: ## Renderer state
164: 
165: - **`components/dataflow/store.ts`**: the editor store (zustand). It holds the workflow tree, the
166:   open workplace (`path`), the selection, React Flow sizes and a notice. Every edit goes through the
167:   core graph rules; errors become a visible notice, never a silent no-op. It lives for the whole app
168:   session, so switching tabs keeps the flow. It isn't saved to disk yet (`workflows.*` is WS1).
169: - **`lib/settings.ts`**: the settings store. It loads `settings.get()` at startup, validates every
170:   change with the `Settings` schema and saves in the background. While main has no settings storage
171:   (`not_implemented`), it keeps the defaults and the Settings page says so.
172: - **zustand 5 rule:** never return a new object or array from a selector (it re-renders forever).
173:   Select existing objects or primitives and derive the rest with `useMemo`.
174: - **Theme:** `lib/theme.ts` sets `<html data-theme>` from Settings (system, light or dark). The CSS
175:   tokens in `globals.css` follow it, so use token classes (`bg-panel`, `text-muted`, …), never hex colors.
176: - **Colorway: BMW M.** The M stripe colours (`m-light` #81C4FF, `m-dark` #16588E, `m-red` #E7222E) on
177:   carbon neutrals. Block groups take them: sources light blue, AI dark blue, HIL red (a person has to
178:   act), Add to Car neutral. `MStripe` (`components/ui/`) marks the active tab. Filled controls use
179:   `bg-brand-fill` so white text stays readable in both themes.
180: 
181: ## AI usage rules
182: 
183: - Use `ctx.llm.generateObject` with a Zod schema for every AI step. Invalid output → throw.
184: - **Never trust model-cited evidence.** The model returns `recordId` and `excerpt`. Code checks that
185:   the excerpt is a verbatim substring of that record, and drops or flags the finding if it isn't.
186: - Batch the records. Use `tier: "fast"` for per-record extraction and `default` for clustering, derivation and challenges.
187: - AI actors in the audit trail record the exact model id returned by the client.
188: - The `mock` provider must return schema-valid, deterministic output so the whole pipeline runs offline.
189: - Prompts live next to the block that uses them (`blocks/src/<block>/<name>.prompt.ts`).
190: 
191: ## Persistence notes (WS1)
192: 
193: - The database lives in the per-user app-data folder (`main/paths.ts`: macOS
194:   `~/Library/Application Support/ReqFlow/data`, Windows `%APPDATA%\ReqFlow\data`, Linux
195:   `~/.config/ReqFlow/data`). `REQFLOW_DATA_DIR` overrides it. Always build paths with `node:path`, never
196:   with string concatenation (Windows uses `\`).
197: - Only one app instance runs at a time (single-instance lock), so only one process writes SQLite.
198: - Workflows are stored whole (the block tree as JSON) and versioned on save.
199: - Requirements are versioned: one row per `(id, version)`. "Current" means the max version.
200: - `audit_events` is insert-only, with no update or delete code path.
201: - Block outputs are stored per `(runId, blockId, port)` as JSON. Imported files are copied into `data/uploads/` inside the data dir.
202: 
203: ## Running, checking, packaging
204: 
205: | Command (repo root) | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
206: | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
207: | `npm run dev`       | Opens the app with hot reload (renderer) and auto-restart (main)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
208: | `npm run smoke`     | Builds, then drives the real app off screen: opens every screen, adds every block, opens an inner workplace, types into fields, connects ports by mouse drag (and checks a loop is refused), walks the settings, switches to dark mode, screenshots each step to `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`, checks the IPC bridge, and exits non-zero on any failed check or renderer error |
209: | `npm run check`     | Typecheck + unit tests + format check                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
210: | `npm run package`   | Installer for the **current** OS in `apps/desktop/release/`: `.exe` (NSIS), `.dmg` or `.AppImage`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
211: 
212: Installers must be built on their own OS (or in a CI matrix later). Builds are unsigned, so macOS
213: Gatekeeper and Windows SmartScreen show a warning on first launch. Code signing is out of scope for the
214: hackathon. Linux CI needs a virtual display (`xvfb-run`) for `smoke`.
</content>

<content>
1: # Workstreams — how to split the work across agents
2: 
3: Each workstream (WS) owns a set of paths, so parallel agents never edit the same files. Everything
4: builds against the contract in `packages/core` (block specs in `blocks.ts`, graph rules in `graph.ts`)
5: and the block contract in `packages/engine/src/block.ts`. UI workstreams use `@reqflow/core/fixtures`
6: until the API is live. Block workstreams test with fixtures and the `mock` LLM.
7: 
8: ## Starting an agent
9: 
10: Paste [AGENT_PROMPT.md](AGENT_PROMPT.md) into the agent, with the workstream filled in. Agents claim
11: work and hand it off in [STATUS.md](STATUS.md), each editing only its own section. **The concrete,
12: ordered task list for every workstream lives in STATUS.md**; this file defines scope, file ownership
13: and "done when".
14: 
15: ## UI agents (WS2–WS4)
16: 
17: The renderer is sandboxed: no Node, no `fs`, no `fetch` to the internet. Reach data only through
18: `api` from `@/lib/api`. Until WS1 implements a method, it throws `ReqflowError` with code
19: `not_implemented`. Show that state, or render `@reqflow/core/fixtures` meanwhile. Reuse the shared
20: controls in `components/ui/` and the design tokens in `globals.css` (light and dark). Check your
21: screens with `npm run smoke` (screenshots land in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`), and extend
22: `apps/desktop/src/main/smoke.ts` (ask WS1/WS0) when you add an interaction worth guarding.
23: 
24: ## Git
25: 
26: Use one branch per workstream (`ws1-engine`, `ws2-editor`, …), ideally in its own `git worktree`. Make small
27: commits (`ws<N>: …`), push right away, and rebase on `main` at least hourly. Merge into `main` through a PR
28: with a merge commit, never a squash, so Entire's checkpoint trailers survive. To add a dependency, add it to **your own** package's
29: `package.json` only. If `package-lock.json` conflicts, run `npm install` again.
30: 
31: ## Phases
32: 
33: 0. **Done (lead):** repo skeleton, the contract (`core`: schemas, block specs, graph rules), the block
34:    contract and registry, the default template, fixtures, the app shell with its three tabs, the Data
35:    Flow editor (structure), the Settings page and the Car placeholder.
36: 1. **Parallel:** WS1–WS8 below.
37: 2. **Integration (lead):** wire services and the registry in `apps/desktop/src/main`, run the default template end
38:    to end with `mock`, then with Claude and the real BMW data, then polish the demo.
39: 
40: ---
41: 
42: ### WS0 — Lead / integrator (main session)
43: 
44: **Owns:** `packages/core/**`, `docs/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, root config files.
45: **Does:** merges branches, reviews and applies contract changes (including block params and ports), runs
46: integration (phase 2) and keeps docs current.
47: 
48: ### WS1 — Engine, persistence & main process
49: 
50: **Owns:** `packages/engine/**`, `packages/db/**`, `apps/desktop/src/main/**`, `apps/desktop/src/preload/**`,
51: `packages/blocks/src/hil/**`, `packages/blocks/src/index.ts`, `packages/blocks/src/templates/**`.
52: **Builds:**
53: 
54: - **First,** the handlers the UIs need: `settings.get/save` (the Settings page already calls them),
55:   `workflows.*` (so the editor can save and load), `files.import` (Raw's file param), and read-only
56:   `requirements.*` / `audit.list` serving the core fixtures until the DB lands.
57: - The executor (see ARCHITECTURE.md → Engine semantics): `validateGraph`, topological run per workplace,
58:   inner workplaces via boundary blocks, merge per input port, per-port output storage, failure →
59:   skipped, pause/resume at HIL, cancel. Wire `BlockContext` (including `ctx.car.add` → DB).
60: - SQLite repositories, versioned requirements, append-only `AuditLogger`, `FileStore`, settings storage.
61: - Every method in `main/handlers.ts` (replace each `notBuilt`), with Zod validation of all arguments. Wire registry, LLM, web search, DB and keychain (`safeStorage`) in `main/`; push run updates via `IPC_EVENTS.runUpdate`.
62: - The HIL block (pause until reviewed, then pass on what the reviewer kept).
63: 
64: **Done when:** executor tests pass with fake blocks (success, failure, multi-port merge, splitter
65: fan-out, inner workplace, pause → resume, cancel). Every IPC method works against SQLite (none left
66: `not_implemented`). A run of fake blocks streams updates to `runs.onUpdate`.
67: 
68: ### WS2 — Data Flow editor UI
69: 
70: **Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/DataflowPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/dataflow/**`.
71: **State today:** palette, workplace (React Flow), blocks with ports, connect with validation, inspector
72: with parameter forms, inner workplaces with breadcrumb, delete with confirmation, snap/minimap from
73: Settings. The flow lives in memory (`components/dataflow/store.ts`).
74: **Builds next:** save/load (`api.workflows.*`, autosave), "New from template" (`api.templates.list()`),
75: undo/redo, copy/paste, a Run button with live status, counts and logs on each block
76: (`api.runs.onUpdate()`), an output inspector (`api.runs.blockOutput()`), and a "waiting for review"
77: banner linking to the Car tab.
78: **Done when:** you can build the default template by hand, save it, reload it, and see run states on the
79: blocks (mocked until WS1 lands).
80: 
81: ### WS3 — Car tab: requirements review & audit UI
82: 
83: **Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/CarPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/car/**`,
84: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/requirements/**`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/audit/**`.
85: **Builds:** the Car tab as the output page: the car (keep the car visual) with its requirements as a
86: list or board, grouped by ranking, with filters and sorting. A detail view shows targets, a score
87: breakdown (factor × weight with notes), priority and rationale, an evidence level badge, assumptions,
88: uncertainties and conflicting evidence, and a drill-down from findings to verbatim excerpts to sources.
89: Add a decision bar (approve / reject / defer / challenge) where rationale is required, inline editing
90: with rationale, a History view, a global audit timeline with before → after diffs and filters, a
91: resume-run action, and export.
92: **Done when:** every field from the briefing's deliverable list is visible for the fixture requirements,
93: and the decision and edit flows call `api.requirements.*`.
94: 
95: ### WS4 — Settings, app shell & packaging
96: 
97: **Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/settings/**`,
98: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/shell/**`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/ui/**` (shared controls),
99: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/lib/settings*.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/lib/theme.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/router.tsx`,
100: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/globals.css`, `apps/desktop/electron-builder.yml`, `apps/desktop/build/**` (app icons).
101: **State today:** bottom tab bar (⌘/Ctrl 1–3), Settings with App, Global parameters, AI & research,
102: Collaboration and About; theme switching (system/light/dark); every change validated with the
103: `Settings` schema. Not saved yet (waits for WS1's `settings.save`).
104: **Builds next:** API-key entry once `settings.setSecret` exists (never display a stored key), a
105: `settings.changed` audit entry once WS1 logs it, the app icon and installer config, demo polish.
106: **Done when:** settings load, validate, save and appear as a `settings.changed` audit event, the shell looks
107: demo-ready, and `npm run package` produces a working installer on your OS.
108: 
109: ### WS5 — Raw block (BMW data ingestion)
110: 
111: **Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/raw/**`, `data/samples/**`.
112: **Builds:** the Raw block. Params (see `BLOCK_SPECS.raw`): Excel upload (`file` = `{ fileId, name }`
113: from `api.files.import()`, `sheet`) or database (`dbType`, `connection`, `query`; never store
114: passwords in params), plus `dataset`. It parses the provided formats (CSV, XLSX and whatever BMW
115: ships: check `data/raw/` once it arrives) into `Source` + `SourceRecord[]` with locators and language.
116: Structured datasets (equipment take rates, sales volumes) also emit deterministic `usage_pattern`
117: findings (for example a high take rate signals a basic expectation) with evidence. Also write
118: synthetic sample files in `data/samples/` that match the real formats. Param changes → request via WS0.
119: **Done when:** each sample dataset ingests in tests, errors name the bad row or column, and no data is dropped silently.
120: 
121: ### WS6 — Research block
122: 
123: **Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/research/**`.
124: **Builds:** the Research block. It turns its params and the scope into queries (competitors in the
125: segment, owner and press reviews, market and technology trends for the horizon), runs them through
126: `ctx.web`, fetches pages and extracts clean text into `SourceRecord`s — the same stream format as Raw —
127: and sets the `Source` kind, publisher, date and **reliability** (with the rule documented). It respects
128: allowed and blocked domains and de-duplicates by URL. Also implement `WebSearch` providers
129: (`anthropic_web_search`, `tavily`) as factories that take keys as arguments (WS1 wires them).
130: **Done when:** a recorded or offline test run produces sources with working URLs and reliability, and failures are logged rather than swallowed.
131: 
132: ### WS7 — AI blocks: AI Filter, AI Splitter, Add to Car
133: 
134: **Owns:** `packages/llm/**`, `packages/blocks/src/ai-filter/**`, `packages/blocks/src/ai-splitter/**`,
135: `packages/blocks/src/add-to-car/**`.
136: **Builds:** an `LlmClient` with a Claude provider and a deterministic `mock` provider (use the `claude-api`
137: skill for SDK details). **AI Filter**: keep items matching the criterion and extract evidence-linked
138: findings (verbatim-excerpt verification; out-of-scope items logged with a reason). **AI Splitter**:
139: route every item to exactly one branch (`out-<i>`); "Split by: Priority" uses WS8's scoring.
140: **Add to Car**: cluster and derive customer-facing, actionable requirements (IDs from
141: `formatRequirementId`, measurable targets, evidence level per the A–D rule, Kano class, assumptions,
142: uncertainties, conflicting findings), set the priority from the input port's ranking, and hand them
143: to `ctx.car.add`. Also export `answerChallenge(...)` for the API's challenge flow.
144: **Done when:** fixture records → filter → splitter → Add to Car runs fully offline with `mock`, all
145: outputs parse against the core schemas, and every finding's excerpt is verified.
146: 
147: ### WS8 — Prioritization
148: 
149: **Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/prioritization/**`.
150: **Builds:** explainable scoring used by the AI Splitter's priority mode. Factors are computed
151: deterministically where possible: customer impact from mentions, sentiment and sales volume; evidence
152: strength from independent sources × reliability and evidence level; competitive gap from
153: `competitor_advantage` findings; trend momentum from `market_trend` findings. The LLM is used only
154: where a judgement is needed (brand fit, ease), always with a one-line note. It uses `weightedTotal`
155: and `priorityForScore` and writes a readable `priorityRationale` naming the top drivers. It also flags
156: "high score, weak evidence".
157: **Done when:** scores are reproducible for the fixtures, changing Settings weights changes the ranking as
158: expected (tested), and each factor has a note a PM can understand.

407: /** Inner-workplace boundary blocks carry the parent port they stand for. */
408: export const BoundaryParams = z.strictObject({ port: z.string().min(1) });
409: export type BoundaryParams = z.infer<typeof BoundaryParams>;
410: 
411: function paramSchema(spec: ParamSpec): z.ZodType {
412:   switch (spec.type) {
413:     case "text":
414:     case "textarea":
415:       return z.string().max(spec.maxLength ?? (spec.type === "text" ? 500 : 5000));
416:     case "number":
417:     case "slider":
418:       return z.number().min(spec.min).max(spec.max);
419:     case "select":
420:       return z.enum(spec.options.map((o) => o.value) as [string, ...string[]]);
421:     case "multiselect": {
422:       const values = spec.options.map((o) => o.value) as [string, ...string[]];
423:       return z
424:         .array(z.enum(values))
425:         .refine((v) => new Set(v).size === v.length, "Each option may be selected only once");
426:     }
427:     case "toggle":
428:       return z.boolean();
429:     case "list":
430:       return z
431:         .array(z.string().trim().min(1, "Entries can't be empty").max(60))
432:         .min(spec.minItems)
433:         .max(spec.maxItems);
434:     case "file":
435:       return FileRef.nullable();
436:   }
437: }
438: 
439: const paramsSchemaCache = new Map<BlockKind, z.ZodType<BlockParams>>();
440: 
441: /** Strict Zod schema for a block's params: unknown keys and wrong types are errors, not dropped. */
442: export function blockParamsSchema(kind: BlockKind): z.ZodType<BlockParams> {
443:   let schema = paramsSchemaCache.get(kind);
444:   if (!schema) {
445:     schema = isBoundaryBlockKind(kind)
446:       ? BoundaryParams
447:       : z.strictObject(
448:           Object.fromEntries(BLOCK_SPECS[kind].params.map((p) => [p.key, paramSchema(p)])),
449:         );
450:     paramsSchemaCache.set(kind, schema);
451:   }
452:   return schema;
453: }
454: 
455: export function defaultBlockParams(kind: PaletteBlockKind): BlockParams {
456:   return Object.fromEntries(
457:     BLOCK_SPECS[kind].params.map((p) => [
458:       p.key,
459:       p.type === "file" ? null : Array.isArray(p.default) ? [...p.default] : p.default,
460:     ]),
461:   );
462: }
463: 
464: /** Throws a ZodError naming the bad field. */
465: export function parseBlockParams(kind: BlockKind, params: unknown): BlockParams {
466:   return blockParamsSchema(kind).parse(params);
467: }
468: 
469: /** Whether a param field is shown, given the block's current params. */
470: export function isParamVisible(spec: ParamSpec, params: BlockParams): boolean {
471:   return !spec.visibleWhen || params[spec.visibleWhen.key] === spec.visibleWhen.equals;
472: }
473: 
474: /**
475:  * Ports of a block. Invalid params fall back to the defaults, so a broken block still renders;
476:  * `validateGraph` reports the invalid params separately.
477:  */
478: export function blockPorts(block: { kind: BlockKind; params: BlockParams }): BlockPorts {
479:   if (block.kind === "block_input") return { inputs: [], outputs: [OUT] };
480:   if (block.kind === "block_output") return { inputs: [IN], outputs: [] };
481:   const parsed = blockParamsSchema(block.kind).safeParse(block.params);
482:   const params = parsed.success ? parsed.data : defaultBlockParams(block.kind);
483:   return BLOCK_SPECS[block.kind].ports(params);
484: }

2: import { Finding, Theme } from "./finding";
3: import { Requirement } from "./requirement";
4: import { Source, SourceRecord } from "./source";
5: 
6: /**
7:  * The single envelope that flows along every workflow edge (n8n-style: one input, one output).
8:  * A node reads the keys it `consumes` and returns the envelope with the keys it `produces` updated.
9:  */
10: export const DATA_KEYS = ["sources", "records", "findings", "themes", "requirements"] as const;
11: export const DataKey = z.enum(DATA_KEYS);
12: export type DataKey = z.infer<typeof DataKey>;
13: 
14: export const PipelineData = z.object({
15:   sources: z.array(Source),
16:   records: z.array(SourceRecord),
17:   findings: z.array(Finding),
18:   themes: z.array(Theme),
19:   requirements: z.array(Requirement),
20: });
21: export type PipelineData = z.infer<typeof PipelineData>;
22: 
23: export function emptyPipelineData(): PipelineData {
24:   return { sources: [], records: [], findings: [], themes: [], requirements: [] };
25: }
26: 
27: function mergeById<T extends { id: string }>(lists: T[][]): T[] {
28:   const byId = new Map<string, T>();
29:   for (const list of lists) for (const item of list) byId.set(item.id, item);
30:   return [...byId.values()];
31: }
32: 
33: /**
34:  * How the engine combines several incoming edges into one node input:
35:  * concatenate per key and de-duplicate by `id`; a later input wins (order = edge order),
36:  * first-seen position is kept so output order stays stable.
37:  */
38: export function mergePipelineData(...parts: PipelineData[]): PipelineData {
39:   return {
40:     sources: mergeById(parts.map((p) => p.sources)),
41:     records: mergeById(parts.map((p) => p.records)),
42:     findings: mergeById(parts.map((p) => p.findings)),
43:     themes: mergeById(parts.map((p) => p.themes)),
44:     requirements: mergeById(parts.map((p) => p.requirements)),
45:   };
46: }
47: 
48: export function countPipelineData(data: PipelineData): Record<DataKey, number> {
49:   return {
50:     sources: data.sources.length,
51:     records: data.records.length,
52:     findings: data.findings.length,
53:     themes: data.themes.length,
54:     requirements: data.requirements.length,
55:   };
56: }

14: /**
15:  * Pure, immutable operations on workflow graphs, shared by the editor and the engine.
16:  * Every operation returns a new graph and throws an Error with a user-readable message on
17:  * invalid input. Nothing is skipped silently.

20: export interface Connection {
21:   source: string;
22:   sourcePort: string;
23:   target: string;
24:   targetPort: string;
25: }
26: 
27: export type ConnectionCheck = { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: string };

29: export interface GraphIssue {
30:   path: string[]; // ids of the blocks whose inner workplaces lead to the problem ([] = top level)
31:   blockId?: string;
32:   edgeId?: string;
33:   message: string;

36: export function emptyGraph(): WorkflowGraph {
37:   return { blocks: [], edges: [] };

40: /** Deterministic, so connecting the same ports twice is detectable by id. */
41: export function edgeId(c: Connection): string {
42:   return `e-${c.source}.${c.sourcePort}-${c.target}.${c.targetPort}`;

45: /** Boundary ids derive from the parent id and port id, which are unique together. */
46: export function boundaryBlockId(parentId: string, portId: string): string {
47:   return `${parentId}--${portId}`;
48: }

50: const BOUNDARY_COLUMN_GAP = 520;
51: const BOUNDARY_ROW_GAP = 120;

53: /** The input and output blocks of an inner workplace: inputs on the left, outputs on the right. */
54: export function boundaryBlocks(parentId: string, ports: BlockPorts): WorkflowBlock[] {
55:   return [
56:     ...ports.inputs.map((port, i): WorkflowBlock => ({
57:       id: boundaryBlockId(parentId, port.id),
58:       kind: "block_input",
59:       label: port.label,
60:       position: { x: 0, y: i * BOUNDARY_ROW_GAP },
61:       params: { port: port.id },
62:     })),
63:     ...ports.outputs.map((port, i): WorkflowBlock => ({
64:       id: boundaryBlockId(parentId, port.id),
65:       kind: "block_output",
66:       label: port.label,
67:       position: { x: BOUNDARY_COLUMN_GAP, y: i * BOUNDARY_ROW_GAP },
68:       params: { port: port.id },
69:     })),
70:   ];

73: /** A new block with default params, and an inner workplace (boundaries only) if the kind has one. */
74: export function createBlock(
75:   kind: PaletteBlockKind,
76:   opts: { id: string; position: { x: number; y: number }; label?: string },
77: ): WorkflowBlock {
78:   const spec = BLOCK_SPECS[kind];
79:   const params = defaultBlockParams(kind);
80:   const block: WorkflowBlock = {
81:     id: opts.id,
82:     kind,
83:     label: opts.label ?? spec.label,
84:     position: opts.position,
85:     params,
86:   };
87:   if (spec.hasInnerWorkplace) {
88:     block.inner = { blocks: boundaryBlocks(opts.id, spec.ports(params)), edges: [] };
89:   }
90:   return block;

93: /** Every block in the tree, depth-first, with the path of the workplace it sits on. */
94: export function* walkBlocks(
95:   graph: WorkflowGraph,
96:   path: string[] = [],
97: ): Generator<{ block: WorkflowBlock; path: string[] }> {
98:   for (const block of graph.blocks) {
99:     yield { block, path };
100:     if (block.inner) yield* walkBlocks(block.inner, [...path, block.id]);
101:   }
102: }

104: /** "Raw", then "Raw 2", "Raw 3", … — unique across the whole workflow. */
105: export function nextBlockLabel(root: WorkflowGraph, base: string): string {
106:   const used = new Set([...walkBlocks(root)].map(({ block }) => block.label));
107:   if (!used.has(base)) return base;
108:   for (let n = 2; ; n++) if (!used.has(`${base} ${n}`)) return `${base} ${n}`;
109: }

111: function requireBlock(graph: WorkflowGraph, id: string): WorkflowBlock {
112:   const block = graph.blocks.find((b) => b.id === id);
113:   if (!block) throw new Error(`Block "${id}" is not on this workplace`);
114:   return block;
115: }
116: 
117: function replaceBlock(graph: WorkflowGraph, next: WorkflowBlock): WorkflowGraph {
118:   return { ...graph, blocks: graph.blocks.map((b) => (b.id === next.id ? next : b)) };
119: }

121: /** The workplace at `path` (block ids from the top level inward). */
122: export function graphAt(root: WorkflowGraph, path: readonly string[]): WorkflowGraph {
123:   let graph = root;
124:   for (const id of path) {
125:     const block = requireBlock(graph, id);
126:     if (!block.inner) throw new Error(`Block "${block.label}" has no inner workplace`);
127:     graph = block.inner;
128:   }

132: /** Replaces the workplace at `path` with `update(workplace)`, copying only the blocks on the path. */
133: export function updateGraphAt(
134:   root: WorkflowGraph,
135:   path: readonly string[],
136:   update: (graph: WorkflowGraph) => WorkflowGraph,
137: ): WorkflowGraph {
138:   if (path.length === 0) return update(root);
139:   const [head, ...rest] = path as [string, ...string[]];
140:   const block = requireBlock(root, head);
141:   if (!block.inner) throw new Error(`Block "${block.label}" has no inner workplace`);
142:   return replaceBlock(root, { ...block, inner: updateGraphAt(block.inner, rest, update) });
143: }

145: /** True when an edge source → target would close a loop (target already reaches source). */
146: export function wouldCreateCycle(graph: WorkflowGraph, source: string, target: string): boolean {
147:   if (source === target) return true;
148:   const next = new Map<string, string[]>();
149:   for (const e of graph.edges) next.set(e.source, [...(next.get(e.source) ?? []), e.target]);
150:   const seen = new Set<string>();
151:   const stack = [target];
152:   while (stack.length) {
153:     const id = stack.pop()!;
154:     if (id === source) return true;
155:     if (seen.has(id)) continue;
156:     seen.add(id);
157:     stack.push(...(next.get(id) ?? []));
158:   }
159:   return false;
160: }

162: export function checkConnection(graph: WorkflowGraph, c: Connection): ConnectionCheck {
163:   const source = graph.blocks.find((b) => b.id === c.source);
164:   const target = graph.blocks.find((b) => b.id === c.target);
165:   if (!source || !target) return { ok: false, reason: "Both blocks must be on this workplace." };
166:   if (source.id === target.id) return { ok: false, reason: "A block can't connect to itself." };
167:   if (!blockPorts(source).outputs.some((p) => p.id === c.sourcePort)) {
168:     return { ok: false, reason: `"${source.label}" has no output "${c.sourcePort}".` };
169:   }
170:   if (!blockPorts(target).inputs.some((p) => p.id === c.targetPort)) {
171:     return { ok: false, reason: `"${target.label}" has no input "${c.targetPort}".` };
172:   }
173:   if (graph.edges.some((e) => e.id === edgeId(c))) {
174:     return { ok: false, reason: "These ports are already connected." };
175:   }
176:   if (wouldCreateCycle(graph, c.source, c.target)) {
177:     return { ok: false, reason: "This connection would create a loop." };
178:   }
179:   return { ok: true };
180: }

182: /** Adds an edge. Several edges may enter one input (merged) or leave one output (fan-out). */
183: export function connect(graph: WorkflowGraph, c: Connection): WorkflowGraph {
184:   const check = checkConnection(graph, c);
185:   if (!check.ok) throw new Error(check.reason);
186:   const edge: WorkflowEdge = {
187:     id: edgeId(c),
188:     source: c.source,
189:     sourcePort: c.sourcePort,
190:     target: c.target,
191:     targetPort: c.targetPort,
192:   };
193:   return { ...graph, edges: [...graph.edges, edge] };
194: }

196: /** Removes blocks and their edges. Unknown ids are ignored, so repeated deletes are harmless. */
197: export function removeBlocks(graph: WorkflowGraph, ids: readonly string[]): WorkflowGraph {
198:   const remove = new Set(ids);
199:   const boundary = graph.blocks.find((b) => remove.has(b.id) && isBoundaryBlockKind(b.kind));
200:   if (boundary) {
201:     throw new Error(`"${boundary.label}" belongs to the parent block's ports and can't be deleted`);
202:   }
203:   return {
204:     blocks: graph.blocks.filter((b) => !remove.has(b.id)),
205:     edges: graph.edges.filter((e) => !remove.has(e.source) && !remove.has(e.target)),
206:   };
207: }
208: 
209: /** Removes edges. Unknown ids are ignored, so repeated deletes are harmless. */
210: export function removeEdges(graph: WorkflowGraph, ids: readonly string[]): WorkflowGraph {
211:   const remove = new Set(ids);
212:   return { ...graph, edges: graph.edges.filter((e) => !remove.has(e.id)) };
213: }

215: export function moveBlock(
216:   graph: WorkflowGraph,
217:   id: string,
218:   position: { x: number; y: number },

221:     throw new Error(`Invalid position for block "${id}"`);

229:   if (trimmed.length > 80) throw new Error("Block names can have at most 80 characters");

233: /** Keeps an inner workplace's boundary blocks in line with the parent's ports. */
234: export function syncBoundaries(
235:   inner: WorkflowGraph,
236:   parentId: string,
237:   ports: BlockPorts,
238: ): WorkflowGraph {
239:   const wanted = boundaryBlocks(parentId, ports);
240:   const wantedIds = new Set(wanted.map((b) => b.id));
241:   const existing = new Map(inner.blocks.map((b) => [b.id, b]));
242:   const stale = inner.blocks
243:     .filter((b) => isBoundaryBlockKind(b.kind) && !wantedIds.has(b.id))
244:     .map((b) => b.id);
245:   const kept = inner.blocks.filter((b) => !stale.includes(b.id));
246:   const merged = kept.map((b) => {
247:     const w = wanted.find((x) => x.id === b.id);
248:     return w ? { ...b, label: w.label } : b;
249:   });
250:   const added = wanted.filter((b) => !existing.has(b.id));
251:   return {
252:     blocks: [...merged, ...added],
253:     edges: inner.edges.filter((e) => !stale.includes(e.source) && !stale.includes(e.target)),

257: /**
258:  * Validates and sets a block's params. Edges on ports that no longer exist (a removed splitter
259:  * branch, say) are removed and returned, so the editor can tell the user.

261: export function setBlockParams(
262:   graph: WorkflowGraph,
263:   id: string,
264:   params: BlockParams,
265: ): { graph: WorkflowGraph; removedEdges: WorkflowEdge[] } {
266:   const block = requireBlock(graph, id);
267:   if (isBoundaryBlockKind(block.kind)) {
268:     throw new Error(`"${block.label}" is a port of the parent block and has no parameters`);
269:   }
270:   const next: WorkflowBlock = { ...block, params: parseBlockParams(block.kind, params) };
271:   const ports = blockPorts(next);
272:   if (next.inner) next.inner = syncBoundaries(next.inner, next.id, ports);
273:   const inputs = new Set(ports.inputs.map((p) => p.id));
274:   const outputs = new Set(ports.outputs.map((p) => p.id));
275:   const removedEdges = graph.edges.filter(
276:     (e) =>
277:       (e.source === id && !outputs.has(e.sourcePort)) ||
278:       (e.target === id && !inputs.has(e.targetPort)),
279:   );
280:   const removed = new Set(removedEdges.map((e) => e.id));
281:   return {
282:     graph: {
283:       blocks: graph.blocks.map((b) => (b.id === id ? next : b)),
284:       edges: graph.edges.filter((e) => !removed.has(e.id)),
285:     },
286:     removedEdges,
287:   };
288: }

290: /** Every problem in the workflow, inner workplaces included. Empty array = valid. */
291: export function validateGraph(root: unknown): GraphIssue[] {
292:   const shape = WorkflowGraph.safeParse(root);
293:   if (!shape.success) {
294:     return shape.error.issues.map((i) => ({
295:       path: [],
296:       message: `${i.path.join(".") || "graph"}: ${i.message}`,
297:     }));
298:   }
299:   const issues: GraphIssue[] = [];
300:   const seen = new Set<string>();
301:   validateLevel(shape.data, [], null, seen, issues);
302:   return issues;
303: }
304: 
305: function validateLevel(
306:   graph: WorkflowGraph,
307:   path: string[],
308:   parent: WorkflowBlock | null,
309:   seen: Set<string>,
310:   issues: GraphIssue[],
311: ): void {
312:   const add = (message: string, ref: { blockId?: string; edgeId?: string } = {}) =>
313:     issues.push({ path, ...ref, message });
314: 
315:   for (const block of graph.blocks) {
316:     const blockId = block.id;
317:     if (seen.has(blockId)) add(`Block id "${blockId}" is used more than once`, { blockId });
318:     seen.add(blockId);
319: 
320:     const params = blockParamsSchema(block.kind).safeParse(block.params);
321:     if (!params.success) {
322:       for (const i of params.error.issues) {
323:         add(`"${block.label}": ${i.path.join(".") || "params"}: ${i.message}`, { blockId });
324:       }
325:     }
326: 
327:     if (isBoundaryBlockKind(block.kind)) {
328:       if (!parent) add(`"${block.label}" can only sit inside an inner workplace`, { blockId });
329:       if (block.inner) add(`"${block.label}" can't have an inner workplace`, { blockId });
330:       continue;
331:     }
332: 
333:     const spec = BLOCK_SPECS[block.kind];
334:     if (spec.hasInnerWorkplace && !block.inner) {
335:       add(`"${block.label}" is missing its inner workplace`, { blockId });
336:     }
337:     if (!spec.hasInnerWorkplace && block.inner) {
338:       add(`"${block.label}" (${spec.label}) can't have an inner workplace`, { blockId });
339:     }
340:     if (block.inner) validateLevel(block.inner, [...path, blockId], block, seen, issues);
341:   }
342: 
343:   if (parent) {
344:     const ports = blockPorts(parent);
345:     for (const [kind, list] of [
346:       ["block_input", ports.inputs],
347:       ["block_output", ports.outputs],
348:     ] as const) {
349:       for (const port of list) {
350:         const count = graph.blocks.filter((b) => b.kind === kind && b.params.port === port.id);
351:         if (count.length !== 1) {
352:           add(`Port "${port.label}" needs exactly one ${kind} block, found ${count.length}`);
353:         }
354:       }
355:       const valid = new Set(list.map((p) => p.id));
356:       for (const b of graph.blocks.filter((b) => b.kind === kind)) {
357:         if (!valid.has(String(b.params.port))) {
358:           add(`"${b.label}" points to a port the parent block doesn't have`, { blockId: b.id });
359:         }
360:       }
361:     }
362:   }
363: 
364:   const edgeIds = new Set<string>();
365:   const blocksById = new Map(graph.blocks.map((b) => [b.id, b]));
366:   for (const edge of graph.edges) {
367:     const ref = { edgeId: edge.id };
368:     if (edgeIds.has(edge.id)) add(`Edge id "${edge.id}" is used more than once`, ref);
369:     edgeIds.add(edge.id);
370:     const source = blocksById.get(edge.source);
371:     const target = blocksById.get(edge.target);
372:     if (!source || !target) {
373:       add(`Edge "${edge.id}" connects a block that isn't on this workplace`, ref);
374:       continue;
375:     }
376:     if (source === target) add(`Edge "${edge.id}" connects "${source.label}" to itself`, ref);
377:     if (!blockPorts(source).outputs.some((p) => p.id === edge.sourcePort)) {
378:       add(`"${source.label}" has no output "${edge.sourcePort}"`, ref);
379:     }
380:     if (!blockPorts(target).inputs.some((p) => p.id === edge.targetPort)) {
381:       add(`"${target.label}" has no input "${edge.targetPort}"`, ref);
382:     }
383:   }
384: 
385:   // Kahn's algorithm: every block must be reachable in topological order.
386:   const indegree = new Map(graph.blocks.map((b) => [b.id, 0]));
387:   for (const e of graph.edges) {
388:     if (indegree.has(e.target)) indegree.set(e.target, indegree.get(e.target)! + 1);
389:   }
390:   const queue = [...indegree].filter(([, d]) => d === 0).map(([id]) => id);
391:   let visited = 0;
392:   while (queue.length) {
393:     const id = queue.shift()!;
394:     visited++;
395:     for (const e of graph.edges.filter((e) => e.source === id)) {
396:       if (!indegree.has(e.target)) continue;
397:       const d = indegree.get(e.target)! - 1;
398:       indegree.set(e.target, d);
399:       if (d === 0) queue.push(e.target);
400:     }
401:   }
402:   if (visited < graph.blocks.length) add("The blocks on this workplace form a loop");
403: }

## What we're building

**ReqFlow** is a hackathon prototype for the BMW challenge _"AI for Product Decision Making"_: a
**native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron, not a web app) with three tabs. On
**Data Flow**, an n8n-style flow of **building blocks** (Custom, Raw, Research, AI Filter, AI Splitter,
HIL, Add to Car; some expand into their own inner workplace) turns customer and market data into
prioritized, evidence-linked car requirements. The **Car** tab shows them for the PM to review, and
**Settings** configures the app, global parameters and collaboration. Full spec: [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md). Your task: [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md).
