## The challenge in brief (from `context/`)

- **Goal:** help BMW product managers define, justify and prioritize **customer-facing requirements
  for the successor** of an existing vehicle, thinking **3–5 years ahead**. The PM stays in control of
  every decision.
- **Vehicles and markets:** the 1, 5 or 7 Series, in Europe, China or the US. Demo **one derivative in one
  market** (ours: 1 Series F70, EU), but don't build a one-off.
- **BMW provides, per vehicle:** customer feedback, equipment data, sales volumes and a customer study.
  We may add web sources such as competitors, reviews and market or technology trends.
- **The app must:** ingest the data and enrich it from the web → extract signals (complaints, unmet needs,
  competitor advantages, trends), **each linked to its sources** → derive clear, actionable, realistic
  requirements → prioritize them with explainable logic → let the PM approve, reject, edit or challenge
  them → record everything in an **audit trail** (who or what, when, and why).
- **Each requirement needs:** a unique ID, an actionable description, linked findings and sources, a
  priority or score, the prioritization rationale, an evidence level, assumptions and uncertainties, and
  a decision status.
- **In scope:** features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment and digital services,
  design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging as the customer experiences them,
  and variants and packages. **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, engineering specs, and
  pricing or business cases (rough effort may be used as a priority factor).
- **Judges value:** trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning, thoughtful prioritization, honest
  handling of uncertainty and **conflicting evidence**, and focus on customer value. Depth in one area
  beats shallow coverage of everything.
- **BMW process we mirror:** situation analysis → structure and context (classify, cluster, dedupe) →
  requirements definition (measurable targets and acceptance criteria) → prioritization (customer and
  business) → documentation and tracking. _"From 1 billion findings to 1,000 requirements to one car."_

## Rules for every agent

1. **Stay in your lane.** Edit only the paths your workstream owns (see WORKSTREAMS.md). Do you need
   something changed elsewhere? Write it in your final report instead of editing it yourself.
2. **`packages/core` is the contract.** Build against it and don't change it on your own. If you need a
   contract change, propose it in your final report. The lead merges contract changes.
3. **No real data in git, logs or transcripts.** BMW files go in `data/raw/` (gitignored). Entire
   publishes session transcripts, so when you inspect them, print only structure and counts (sheet
   and column names, row counts), never cell values, and never send them to delegated agents.
   Committed tests use synthetic data (`@reqflow/core/fixtures`, `data/samples/`). Never commit or
   print API keys.
4. **No silent failures.** Validate inputs with the Zod schemas, throw clear errors, and never invent
   sources or evidence. Every finding needs a verbatim excerpt.
5. **AI never decides.** Only a human sets `approved`, `rejected` or `deferred`. Every change to a
   requirement writes an AuditEvent.
6. **Prove it works.** Add colocated `*.test.ts` files. Before you report done, run
   `npm run typecheck && npm test` from the repo root. For UI work, also run `npm run smoke` and look at
   the screenshots in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`.
7. **Respect the process split.** UI code (renderer) has no Node, no `fs` and no network. It talks to the
   main process only through `api` from `@/lib/api` (contract: `packages/core/src/ipc.ts`). Data, AI
   calls, files and API keys live in the main process. Build paths with `node:path` so they work on Windows.
8. **Sessions are tracked with [Entire](https://github.com/entireio/cli).** Commit with plain `git`.
   Entire attaches your session to each commit as a checkpoint and pushes it on `git push`. Don't
   remove its hooks (`.claude/settings.json`, `.git/hooks`) and never put secrets in prompts.

9. **Hand off in [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).** Claim your workstream there when you start; your
   tasks are the checklist in its section, in priority order. Update your own section (and only that
   one) when you finish a slice, get blocked or stop: tick done tasks, add a log entry. The next agent
   starts from it. The repo and Entire transcripts are **public**, so never paste keys or BMW data anywhere.

## Commands (repo root, Node ≥ 22.13; works on Windows, macOS, Linux)

```
npm install          # once
npm run dev          # opens the desktop app with hot reload
npm run smoke        # builds, screenshots every screen, checks the IPC bridge
npm test             # vitest, all packages
npm run typecheck    # all workspaces
npm run format       # prettier
npm run package      # installer for your OS → apps/desktop/release/
```

1: # AGENTS.md — read this first
2: 
3: ## What we're building
4: 
5: **ReqFlow** is a hackathon prototype for the BMW challenge _"AI for Product Decision Making"_: a
6: **native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron, not a web app) with three tabs. On
7: **Data Flow**, an n8n-style flow of **building blocks** (Custom, Raw, Research, AI Filter, AI Splitter,
8: HIL, Add to Car; some expand into their own inner workplace) turns customer and market data into
9: prioritized, evidence-linked car requirements. The **Car** tab shows them for the PM to review, and
10: **Settings** configures the app, global parameters and collaboration. Full spec: [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md). Your task: [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md).
11: Current state and handoffs: [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).
12: 
13: ## The challenge in brief (from `context/`)
14: 
15: - **Goal:** help BMW product managers define, justify and prioritize **customer-facing requirements
16:   for the successor** of an existing vehicle, thinking **3–5 years ahead**. The PM stays in control of
17:   every decision.
18: - **Vehicles and markets:** the 1, 5 or 7 Series, in Europe, China or the US. Demo **one derivative in one
19:   market** (ours: 1 Series F70, EU), but don't build a one-off.
20: - **BMW provides, per vehicle:** customer feedback, equipment data, sales volumes and a customer study.
21:   We may add web sources such as competitors, reviews and market or technology trends.
22: - **The app must:** ingest the data and enrich it from the web → extract signals (complaints, unmet needs,
23:   competitor advantages, trends), **each linked to its sources** → derive clear, actionable, realistic
24:   requirements → prioritize them with explainable logic → let the PM approve, reject, edit or challenge
25:   them → record everything in an **audit trail** (who or what, when, and why).
26: - **Each requirement needs:** a unique ID, an actionable description, linked findings and sources, a
27:   priority or score, the prioritization rationale, an evidence level, assumptions and uncertainties, and
28:   a decision status.
29: - **In scope:** features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment and digital services,
30:   design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging as the customer experiences them,
31:   and variants and packages. **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, engineering specs, and
32:   pricing or business cases (rough effort may be used as a priority factor).
33: - **Judges value:** trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning, thoughtful prioritization, honest
34:   handling of uncertainty and **conflicting evidence**, and focus on customer value. Depth in one area
35:   beats shallow coverage of everything.
36: - **BMW process we mirror:** situation analysis → structure and context (classify, cluster, dedupe) →
37:   requirements definition (measurable targets and acceptance criteria) → prioritization (customer and
38:   business) → documentation and tracking. _"From 1 billion findings to 1,000 requirements to one car."_
39: 
40: ## Rules for every agent
41: 
42: 1. **Stay in your lane.** Edit only the paths your workstream owns (see WORKSTREAMS.md). Do you need
43:    something changed elsewhere? Write it in your final report instead of editing it yourself.
44: 2. **`packages/core` is the contract.** Build against it and don't change it on your own. If you need a
45:    contract change, propose it in your final report. The lead merges contract changes.
46: 3. **No real data in git, logs or transcripts.** BMW files go in `data/raw/` (gitignored). Entire
47:    publishes session transcripts, so when you inspect them, print only structure and counts (sheet
48:    and column names, row counts), never cell values, and never send them to delegated agents.
49:    Committed tests use synthetic data (`@reqflow/core/fixtures`, `data/samples/`). Never commit or
50:    print API keys.
51: 4. **No silent failures.** Validate inputs with the Zod schemas, throw clear errors, and never invent
52:    sources or evidence. Every finding needs a verbatim excerpt.
53: 5. **AI never decides.** Only a human sets `approved`, `rejected` or `deferred`. Every change to a
54:    requirement writes an AuditEvent.
55: 6. **Prove it works.** Add colocated `*.test.ts` files. Before you report done, run
56:    `npm run typecheck && npm test` from the repo root. For UI work, also run `npm run smoke` and look at
57:    the screenshots in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`.
58: 7. **Respect the process split.** UI code (renderer) has no Node, no `fs` and no network. It talks to the
59:    main process only through `api` from `@/lib/api` (contract: `packages/core/src/ipc.ts`). Data, AI
60:    calls, files and API keys live in the main process. Build paths with `node:path` so they work on Windows.
61: 8. **Sessions are tracked with [Entire](https://github.com/entireio/cli).** Commit with plain `git`.
62:    Entire attaches your session to each commit as a checkpoint and pushes it on `git push`. Don't
63:    remove its hooks (`.claude/settings.json`, `.git/hooks`) and never put secrets in prompts.
64: 
65: 9. **Hand off in [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).** Claim your workstream there when you start; your
66:    tasks are the checklist in its section, in priority order. Update your own section (and only that
67:    one) when you finish a slice, get blocked or stop: tick done tasks, add a log entry. The next agent
68:    starts from it. The repo and Entire transcripts are **public**, so never paste keys or BMW data anywhere.
69: 
70: ## Commands (repo root, Node ≥ 22.13; works on Windows, macOS, Linux)
71: 
72: ```
73: npm install          # once
74: npm run dev          # opens the desktop app with hot reload
75: npm run smoke        # builds, screenshots every screen, checks the IPC bridge
76: npm test             # vitest, all packages
77: npm run typecheck    # all workspaces
78: npm run format       # prettier
79: npm run package      # installer for your OS → apps/desktop/release/
80: ```

1: import { z } from "zod";
2: 
3: /**
4:  * Explainable prioritization: every factor is 0–5 where HIGHER always means "more worth doing".
5:  * total = 100 × Σ(weight × value) / (5 × Σ weight)   →   0–100
6:  * Weights and priority thresholds live in Settings.scoring and are recorded with each score.
7:  */
8: export const ScoreFactor = z.enum([
9:   "customer_impact", // how strongly and how many customers are affected
10:   "evidence_strength", // number, independence and reliability of supporting sources
11:   "competitive_gap", // competitors offer it / do it better
12:   "trend_momentum", // expected relevance when the successor launches (3–5 years)
13:   "brand_fit", // fit with BMW brand promise (premium, driving pleasure, …)
14:   "ease", // inverse of rough effort/cost — the only business factor allowed by the briefing
15: ]);
16: export type ScoreFactor = z.infer<typeof ScoreFactor>;
17: 
18: export const SCORE_FACTOR_LABELS: Record<ScoreFactor, string> = {
19:   customer_impact: "Customer impact",
20:   evidence_strength: "Evidence strength",
21:   competitive_gap: "Competitive gap",
22:   trend_momentum: "Trend momentum",
23:   brand_fit: "Brand fit",
24:   ease: "Ease of delivery (inverse effort)",
25: };
26: 
27: /** MoSCoW priority bands. */
28: export const Priority = z.enum(["must", "should", "could", "wont"]);
29: export type Priority = z.infer<typeof Priority>;
30: 
31: export const ScoreWeights = z.record(ScoreFactor, z.number().min(0).max(10));
32: export type ScoreWeights = z.infer<typeof ScoreWeights>;
33: 
34: /** Minimum total score for each band; below `could` → "wont". */
35: export const PriorityThresholds = z
36:   .object({
37:     must: z.number().min(0).max(100),
38:     should: z.number().min(0).max(100),
39:     could: z.number().min(0).max(100),
40:   })
41:   .refine((t) => t.must > t.should && t.should > t.could, {
42:     message: "Thresholds must satisfy must > should > could",
43:   });
44: export type PriorityThresholds = z.infer<typeof PriorityThresholds>;
45: 
46: export const FactorScore = z.object({
47:   value: z.number().min(0).max(5),
48:   weight: z.number().min(0).max(10), // weight at scoring time (snapshot of Settings)
49:   note: z.string().min(1), // one-line justification, shown to the PM
50: });
51: export type FactorScore = z.infer<typeof FactorScore>;
52: 
53: export const ScoreBreakdown = z.object({
54:   factors: z.record(ScoreFactor, FactorScore),
55:   total: z.number().min(0).max(100),
56:   suggestedPriority: Priority, // what the score says; Requirement.priority may be overridden by the PM
57:   method: z.string().min(1), // versioned, e.g. "weighted-sum@1"
58:   scoredAt: z.iso.datetime(),
59: });
60: export type ScoreBreakdown = z.infer<typeof ScoreBreakdown>;
61: 
62: /** The documented formula: 100 × Σ(weight × value) / (5 × Σ weight), rounded to one decimal. */
63: export function weightedTotal(
64:   values: Record<ScoreFactor, number>,
65:   weights: Record<ScoreFactor, number>,
66: ): number {
67:   let num = 0;
68:   let den = 0;
69:   for (const f of ScoreFactor.options) {
70:     const v = values[f];
71:     const w = weights[f];
72:     if (!(v >= 0 && v <= 5)) throw new RangeError(`Factor ${f} must be within 0–5, got ${v}`);
73:     if (!(w >= 0)) throw new RangeError(`Weight for ${f} must be ≥ 0, got ${w}`);
74:     num += w * v;
75:     den += 5 * w;
76:   }
77:   if (den === 0) throw new RangeError("At least one score weight must be > 0");
78:   return Math.round((1000 * num) / den) / 10;
79: }
80: 
81: export function priorityForScore(total: number, t: PriorityThresholds): Priority {
82:   if (total >= t.must) return "must";
83:   if (total >= t.should) return "should";
84:   if (total >= t.could) return "could";
85:   return "wont";
86: }
</content>

59: export function topologicalSortBlocks(graph: WorkflowGraph): WorkflowBlock[] {
60:   const blockMap = new Map<string, WorkflowBlock>(graph.blocks.map((b) => [b.id, b]));
61:   const inDegree = new Map<string, number>(graph.blocks.map((b) => [b.id, 0]));
62: 
63:   for (const edge of graph.edges) {
64:     if (inDegree.has(edge.target)) {
65:       inDegree.set(edge.target, inDegree.get(edge.target)! + 1);
66:     }
67:   }
68: 
69:   const queue: string[] = [];
70:   for (const [id, deg] of inDegree.entries()) {
71:     if (deg === 0) queue.push(id);
72:   }
73: 
74:   const sorted: WorkflowBlock[] = [];
75:   while (queue.length > 0) {
76:     const id = queue.shift()!;
77:     const block = blockMap.get(id);
78:     if (block) sorted.push(block);
79: 
80:     for (const edge of graph.edges.filter((e) => e.source === id)) {
81:       if (inDegree.has(edge.target)) {
82:         const deg = inDegree.get(edge.target)! - 1;
83:         inDegree.set(edge.target, deg);
84:         if (deg === 0) queue.push(edge.target);
85:       }
86:     }
87:   }
88: 
89:   if (sorted.length < graph.blocks.length) {
90:     throw new EngineError("The blocks on this workplace form a loop");
91:   }
92: 
93:   return sorted;
94: }

101:       if (b.inner) recurse(b.inner);

134: export function createDataflowStore(initial: WorkflowGraph = emptyGraph()) {
135:   let noticeId = 0;

137:   return createStore<DataflowState>()((set, get) => {
138:     /** Runs `update` on the open workplace; on error, shows it and leaves the state unchanged. */
139:     const edit = (update: (graph: WorkflowGraph) => WorkflowGraph): boolean => {
140:       try {
141:         const current = selectWorkplace(get());
142:         const next = update(current);
143:         if (next !== current) set({ root: updateGraphAt(get().root, get().path, () => next) });
144:         return true;
145:       } catch (err) {
146:         get().notify("error", message(err));
147:         return false;
148:       }
149:     };
150: 
151:     return {
152:       root: initial,
153:       path: [],
154:       selectedBlockIds: [],
155:       selectedEdgeIds: [],
156:       measured: {},
157:       notice: null,
158:       report: null,
159: 
160:       addBlock(kind, position) {
161:         const id = newBlockId(kind);
162:         const label = nextBlockLabel(get().root, BLOCK_SPECS[kind].label);
163:         const block = createBlock(kind, { id, label, position });
164:         if (edit((g) => ({ ...g, blocks: [...g.blocks, block] }))) {
165:           set({ selectedBlockIds: [id], selectedEdgeIds: [] });
166:         }
167:         return id;
168:       },
169: 
170:       applyNodeChanges(changes) {
171:         let selected = new Set(get().selectedBlockIds);
172:         let measured = get().measured;
173:         const removed: string[] = [];
174:         const ok = edit((graph) => {
175:           let g = graph;
176:           for (const c of changes) {
177:             if (c.type === "position" && c.position) g = moveBlock(g, c.id, c.position);
178:             else if (c.type === "dimensions" && c.dimensions) {
179:               measured = { ...measured, [c.id]: c.dimensions };
180:             } else if (c.type === "select") {
181:               selected = new Set(selected);
182:               if (c.selected) selected.add(c.id);
183:               else selected.delete(c.id);
184:             } else if (c.type === "remove") removed.push(c.id);
185:           }
186:           return removed.length ? removeBlocks(g, removed) : g;
187:         });
188:         if (!ok) return;
189:         for (const id of removed) selected.delete(id);
190:         set({ selectedBlockIds: [...selected], measured });
191:       },
192: 
193:       applyEdgeChanges(changes) {
194:         let selected = new Set(get().selectedEdgeIds);
195:         const removed = changes.filter((c) => c.type === "remove").map((c) => c.id);
196:         for (const c of changes) {
197:           if (c.type !== "select") continue;
198:           selected = new Set(selected);
199:           if (c.selected) selected.add(c.id);
200:           else selected.delete(c.id);
201:         }
202:         if (removed.length && !edit((g) => removeEdges(g, removed))) return;
203:         for (const id of removed) selected.delete(id);
204:         set({ selectedEdgeIds: [...selected] });
205:       },
206: 
207:       checkConnection(connection) {
208:         const c = toCoreConnection(connection);
209:         if (!c) return { ok: false, reason: "Connect an output port to an input port." };
210:         return checkConnection(selectWorkplace(get()), c);
211:       },
212: 
213:       connect(connection) {
214:         const c = toCoreConnection(connection);
215:         if (!c) {
216:           get().notify("error", "Connect an output port to an input port.");
217:           return false;
218:         }
219:         return edit((g) => connectPorts(g, c));
220:       },
221: 
222:       deleteSelection() {
223:         const graph = selectWorkplace(get());
224:         const blocks = graph.blocks
225:           .filter((b) => get().selectedBlockIds.includes(b.id) && !isBoundaryBlockKind(b.kind))
226:           .map((b) => b.id);
227:         const edges = get().selectedEdgeIds;
228:         if (edit((g) => removeEdges(removeBlocks(g, blocks), edges))) {
229:           set({ selectedBlockIds: [], selectedEdgeIds: [] });
230:         }
231:       },
232: 
233:       setParams(blockId, params) {

235:         const block = graph.blocks.find((b) => b.id === blockId);
236:         if (!block) return `Block "${blockId}" is not on this workplace`;
237:         try {
238:           const result = setBlockParams(graph, blockId, params);
239:           set({ root: updateGraphAt(get().root, get().path, () => result.graph) });
240:           const n = result.removedEdges.length;
241:           if (n > 0) {
242:             get().notify(
243:               "info",
244:               `Removed ${n} connection${n === 1 ? "" : "s"} from ports that no longer exist.`,
245:             );
246:           }

258:         } catch (err) {

260:         }
261:       },
262: 
263:       selectBlock(blockId) {

265:       },
266:

269:         if (!block?.inner) {
270:           get().notify("error", `"${block?.label ?? blockId}" has no inner workplace.`);
271:           return;
272:         }
273:         set({ path: [...get().path, blockId], selectedBlockIds: [], selectedEdgeIds: [] });
274:       },
275: 
276:       goTo(depth) {
277:         if (depth < 0 || depth > get().path.length) return;
278:         set({ path: get().path.slice(0, depth), selectedBlockIds: [], selectedEdgeIds: [] });
279:       },
280: 
281:       openReport(blockId) {

283:         if (!block) {

285:           return;

54:     js<boolean>(

56:     );

62:     frame = image;

79:     });

81:     wc.sendInputEvent({ type: "mouseDown", ...a, button: "left", clickCount: 1 });

282:   private async executeWorkplace(
283:     run: WorkflowRun,
284:     graph: WorkflowGraph,
285:     parentInputs: Record<string, PipelineData>,
286:     settings: Settings,
287:     signal: AbortSignal,
288:     resumedExecution: boolean,
289:   ): Promise<{ status: "ok"; outputs: Record<string, PipelineData> } | { status: "paused" }> {
290:     const sorted = topologicalSortBlocks(graph);
291: 
292:     for (let i = 0; i < sorted.length; i++) {
293:       if (signal.aborted) {
294:         run.status = "cancelled";
295:         run.finishedAt = new Date().toISOString();
296:         this.emitUpdate(run);
297:         return { status: "paused" };
298:       }
299: 
300:       const block = sorted[i]!;
301:       const blockRun = run.blockRuns.find((br) => br.blockId === block.id)!;
302: 
303:       if (resumedExecution && blockRun.status === "succeeded") {
304:         continue;
305:       }
306: 
307:       const incomingEdges = graph.edges.filter((e) => e.target === block.id);
308:       const parentRuns = incomingEdges.map((e) =>
309:         run.blockRuns.find((br) => br.blockId === e.source),
310:       );
311:       if (parentRuns.some((p) => p && (p.status === "failed" || p.status === "skipped"))) {
312:         blockRun.status = "skipped";
313:         this.emitUpdate(run);
314:         continue;
315:       }
316: 
317:       const blockInputs: Record<string, PipelineData> = {};
318: 
319:       if (block.kind === "block_input") {
320:         const portId = (block.params as { port?: string }).port ?? "in";
321:         const incomingData = parentInputs[portId] ?? emptyPipelineData();
322:         blockInputs.in = incomingData;
323:       } else {
324:         for (const edge of incomingEdges) {
325:           const sourceOutputs = (await this.getBlockOutput(run.id, edge.source)) ?? {};
326:           const carriedData = sourceOutputs[edge.sourcePort] ?? emptyPipelineData();
327:           if (!blockInputs[edge.targetPort]) {
328:             blockInputs[edge.targetPort] = carriedData;
329:           } else {
330:             blockInputs[edge.targetPort] = mergePipelineData(
331:               blockInputs[edge.targetPort]!,
332:               carriedData,
333:             );
334:           }
335:         }
336:       }
337: 
338:       const isResumingThisBlock = resumedExecution && blockRun.status === "waiting_for_review";
339: 
340:       blockRun.status = "running";
341:       blockRun.startedAt = blockRun.startedAt ?? new Date().toISOString();
342:       this.emitUpdate(run);
343: 
344:       const ctx: BlockContext = {
345:         runId: run.id,
346:         blockId: block.id,
347:         scope: run.scope,
348:         settings,
349:         llm: this.options.services.llm,

351:         files: this.options.services.files,
352:         web: this.options.services.web,
353:         car: this.options.services.car,
354:         log: (msg) => {
355:           blockRun.logs.push({ at: new Date().toISOString(), message: msg });
356:           this.emitUpdate(run);
357:         },
358:         progress: (frac, msg) => {
359:           blockRun.progress = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, frac));
360:           if (msg) blockRun.logs.push({ at: new Date().toISOString(), message: msg });
361:           this.emitUpdate(run);
362:         },
363:         signal,
364:         resumed: isResumingThisBlock,
365:       };
366: 
367:       try {
368:         let blockOutputs: Record<string, PipelineData> = {};
369: 
370:         if (block.kind === "block_input") {
371:           blockOutputs = { out: blockInputs.in ?? emptyPipelineData() };
372:         } else if (block.kind === "block_output") {
373:           blockOutputs = { in: blockInputs.in ?? emptyPipelineData() };
374:         } else if (block.inner && block.inner.blocks.length > 0) {
375:           const subflowRes = await this.executeWorkplace(
376:             run,
377:             block.inner,
378:             blockInputs,
379:             settings,
380:             signal,
381:             resumedExecution,
382:           );
383:           if (subflowRes.status === "paused") {
384:             return { status: "paused" };
385:           }
386:           blockOutputs = subflowRes.outputs;
387:         } else {

389:           const validatedParams = parseBlockParams(block.kind, block.params);

391: 
392:           if (signal.aborted) {
393:             run.status = "cancelled";
394:             run.finishedAt = new Date().toISOString();
395:             this.emitUpdate(run);
396:             return { status: "paused" };
397:           }
398:

411:

1: import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
2: import { join } from "node:path";
3: import type { SecretName, SecretStatus } from "@reqflow/core/ipc";
4: 
5: const ENV_VAR_MAP: Record<SecretName, string> = {
6:   anthropic_api_key: "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",
7:   tavily_api_key: "TAVILY_API_KEY",
8: };
9: 
10: async function getSafeStorage() {
11:   try {
12:     const electron = await import("electron");
13:     return electron.safeStorage;
14:   } catch {
15:     return undefined;
16:   }
17: }
18: 
19: export class SecretsStore {
20:   private readonly filePath: string;
21: 
22:   constructor(dataDir: string) {
23:     this.filePath = join(dataDir, "secrets.json");
24:   }
25: 
26:   private readAll(): Record<string, string> {
27:     if (!existsSync(this.filePath)) return {};
28:     try {
29:       const content = readFileSync(this.filePath, "utf8");
30:       return JSON.parse(content) as Record<string, string>;
31:     } catch {
32:       return {};
33:     }
34:   }
35: 
36:   private writeAll(data: Record<string, string>): void {
37:     writeFileSync(this.filePath, JSON.stringify(data, null, 2), "utf8");
38:   }
39: 
40:   async getSecret(name: SecretName): Promise<string | null> {
41:     const all = this.readAll();
42:     const stored = all[name];
43:     if (stored) {
44:       try {
45:         const safeStorage = await getSafeStorage();
46:         if (safeStorage && safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()) {
47:           const buf = Buffer.from(stored, "base64");
48:           return safeStorage.decryptString(buf);
49:         }
50:         return Buffer.from(stored, "base64").toString("utf8");
51:       } catch {
52:         // Fallback / corrupted
53:       }
54:     }
55: 
56:     const envVar = ENV_VAR_MAP[name];
57:     if (envVar && process.env[envVar]) {
58:       return process.env[envVar]!;
59:     }
60: 
61:     return null;
62:   }
63: 
64:   async setSecret(name: SecretName, value: string | null): Promise<void> {
65:     const all = this.readAll();
66:     if (value === null || value === undefined || value.trim() === "") {
67:       delete all[name];
68:     } else {
69:       const safeStorage = await getSafeStorage();
70:       if (safeStorage && safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()) {
71:         const encrypted = safeStorage.encryptString(value);
72:         all[name] = encrypted.toString("base64");
73:       } else {
74:         all[name] = Buffer.from(value, "utf8").toString("base64");
75:       }
76:     }
77:     this.writeAll(all);
78:   }
79: 
80:   async getStatus(): Promise<SecretStatus> {
81:     const all = this.readAll();
82:     const result: SecretStatus = {
83:       anthropic_api_key: { configured: false, source: null },
84:       tavily_api_key: { configured: false, source: null },
85:     };
86: 
87:     const keys: SecretName[] = ["anthropic_api_key", "tavily_api_key"];
88:     for (const key of keys) {
89:       if (all[key]) {
90:         result[key] = { configured: true, source: "keychain" };
91:       } else {
92:         const envVar = ENV_VAR_MAP[key];
93:         if (envVar && process.env[envVar]) {
94:           result[key] = { configured: true, source: "env" };
95:         } else {
96:           result[key] = { configured: false, source: null };
97:         }
98:       }
99:     }
100: 
101:     return result;
102:   }
103: }

## What we're building

**ReqFlow** is a hackathon prototype for the BMW challenge _"AI for Product Decision Making"_: a
**native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron, not a web app) with three tabs. On

## The challenge in brief (from `context/`)

- **Goal:** help BMW product managers define, justify and prioritize **customer-facing requirements
  for the successor** of an existing vehicle, thinking **3–5 years ahead**. The PM stays in control of
  every decision.
- **Vehicles and markets:** the 1, 5 or 7 Series, in Europe, China or the US. Demo **one derivative in one

  competitor advantages, trends), **each linked to its sources** → derive clear, actionable, realistic
  requirements → prioritize them with explainable logic → let the PM approve, reject, edit or challenge
  them → record everything in an **audit trail** (who or what, when, and why).
- **Each requirement needs:** a unique ID, an actionable description, linked findings and sources, a
  priority or score, the prioritization rationale, an evidence level, assumptions and uncertainties, and

71:     if (deg === 0) queue.push(id);
72:   }
73: 
74:   const sorted: WorkflowBlock[] = [];
75:   while (queue.length > 0) {
76:     const id = queue.shift()!;
77:     const block = blockMap.get(id);
78:     if (block) sorted.push(block);
79: 
80:     for (const edge of graph.edges.filter((e) => e.source === id)) {
81:       if (inDegree.has(edge.target)) {
82:         const deg = inDegree.get(edge.target)! - 1;
83:         inDegree.set(edge.target, deg);
84:         if (deg === 0) queue.push(edge.target);
85:       }
86:     }
87:   }
88: 
89:   if (sorted.length < graph.blocks.length) {
90:     throw new EngineError("The blocks on this workplace form a loop");
91:   }
92: 
93:   return sorted;

109:   const downstream = new Set<string>();

112:   for (const b of graph.blocks) adj.set(b.id, []);
113:   for (const e of graph.edges) adj.get(e.source)?.push(e.target);

118:     const neighbors = adj.get(curr) ?? [];
119:     for (const next of neighbors) {
120:       if (!downstream.has(next)) {

122:         queue.push(next);
123:       }

28: /** Race even injected transports that ignore AbortSignal; always remove the listener. */
29: async function cancellable<T>(work: () => Promise<T>, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<T> {
30:   signal?.throwIfAborted();
31:   if (!signal) return work();
32:   let listener: () => void = () => {};
33:   const aborted = new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {
34:     listener = () => reject(signal.reason);
35:     signal.addEventListener("abort", listener, { once: true });
36:   });
37:   try {
38:     const value = await Promise.race([work(), aborted]);
39:     signal.throwIfAborted();
40:     return value;
41:   } finally {
42:     signal.removeEventListener("abort", listener);
43:   }
44: }
45: 
46: /** Minimal Messages API client. No retries, secret discovery, SDK, or live calls at construction. */
47: export function createLlmClient(
48:   settings: AppSettings["llm"],
49:   options: LlmClientOptions = {},
50: ): LlmClient {
51:   const config = Settings.shape.llm.parse(settings);
52:   if (config.provider === "mock") {
53:     return {
54:       async generateObject(request) {
55:         request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
56:         const checked = Request.parse(request);
57:         const object = request.schema.parse(mockObject(checked.prompt));
58:         request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
59:         return { object, model: `mock:${checked.tier ?? "default"}` };
60:       },
61:       async generateText(request) {
62:         request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
63:         const checked = Request.parse(request);
64:         return {
65:           text: "[MOCK] Offline provider does not generate prose.",
66:           model: `mock:${checked.tier ?? "default"}`,
67:         };
68:       },
69:     };
70:   }
71: 
72:   const apiKey = options.apiKey?.trim();
73:   if (!apiKey) throw new Error("Anthropic API key is required; supply it from the secret store.");
74:   const fetch = options.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch;
75: 
76:   async function message(request: LlmTextRequest, schema?: Record<string, unknown>) {
77:     request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
78:     const checked = Request.parse(request);
79:     const body = {
80:       model: checked.tier === "fast" ? config.fastModel : config.model,
81:       max_tokens: 8192,
82:       temperature: config.temperature,
83:       ...(checked.system !== undefined ? { system: checked.system } : {}),
84:       messages: [{ role: "user", content: checked.prompt }],
85:       ...(schema ? { output_config: { format: { type: "json_schema", schema } } } : {}),
86:     };
87:     const result = await cancellable(async () => {
88:       const response = await fetch("https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages", {
89:         method: "POST",
90:         headers: {
91:           "content-type": "application/json",
92:           "anthropic-version": "2023-06-01",
93:           "x-api-key": apiKey!,
94:         },
95:         body: JSON.stringify(body),
96:         signal: request.signal,
97:       });
98:       // Error bodies can contain secrets or request text. Do not include them in errors/logs.
99:       if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Anthropic request failed (HTTP ${response.status})`);
100:       return Message.parse(await response.json());
101:     }, request.signal);
102:     return { text: result.content.map((part) => part.text).join(""), model: result.model };
103:   }
104: 
105:   return {
106:     async generateObject(request) {
107:       request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
108:       // Unsupported Zod schemas fail explicitly rather than silently losing validation constraints.
109:       const jsonSchema = z.toJSONSchema(request.schema);
110:       delete jsonSchema.$schema;
111:       const result = await message(request, jsonSchema);
112:       let raw: unknown;
113:       try {
114:         raw = JSON.parse(result.text);
115:       } catch {
116:         throw new Error("Anthropic structured response is not valid JSON");
117:       }
118:       const object = request.schema.parse(raw);
119:       request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
120:       return { object, model: result.model };
121:     },
122:     generateText: (request) => message(request),
123:   };
124: }

**Location:** `packages/llm/src/index.ts:109–111`; `packages/blocks/src/ai-splitter/protocol.ts:45–48`

21: /** Evidence claims need an available ID and verbatim quotation; unmeasured judgement is an assumption. */
22: function validateNote(note: string, entry: PromptItem, factor: ScoreFactor): void {
23:   if (/^(Assumption:|MOCK assumption:)/i.test(note)) return;
24:   const match = /^Evidence:\s*(src_\S+|rec_\S+)\s*\|\s*("(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*")\s*\|\s*\S.+$/i.exec(
25:     note,
26:   );
27:   if (!match)
28:     throw new Error(
29:       `Provisional ${entry.id} factor ${factor} note must identify Assumption: or Evidence: ID | "verbatim excerpt" | judgement`,
30:     );
31:   const id = match[1]!;
32:   let excerpt: string;
33:   try {
34:     excerpt = JSON.parse(match[2]!) as string;
35:   } catch {
36:     throw new Error(`Provisional ${entry.id} factor ${factor} evidence quote must be JSON-quoted`);
37:   }
38:   const records = [
39:     ...entry.context.records,
40:     ...(entry.layer === "records" ? [entry.item as PipelineData["records"][number]] : []),
41:   ];
42:   const findings = [
43:     ...entry.context.findings,
44:     ...(entry.layer === "findings" ? [entry.item as PipelineData["findings"][number]] : []),
45:   ];
46:   const texts = [
47:     ...records
48:       .filter((record) => record.id === id || record.sourceId === id)
49:       .map((record) => record.text),
50:     ...findings.flatMap((finding) =>
51:       finding.evidence
52:         .filter((ref) => ref.sourceId === id || ref.recordId === id)
53:         .map((ref) => ref.excerpt),
54:     ),
55:   ];
56:   if (!excerpt.trim() || !texts.some((text) => text.includes(excerpt))) {
57:     throw new Error(
58:       `Provisional ${entry.id} factor ${factor} cites unknown evidence or a non-verbatim excerpt`,
59:     );
60:   }
61: }

63: /** Named bands only. Contiguous upper bands may coarsen omitted lower bands, always with a log. */
64: export function priorityBranches(labels: string[]) {
65:   const map = new Map<Priority, number>();
66:   for (const [index, label] of labels.entries()) {
67:     const normalized = label
68:       .toLowerCase()
69:       .replace(/[\s'’\-]/g, "")
70:       .replace(/have$/, "");
71:     const parsed = Priority.safeParse(normalized);
72:     if (!parsed.success || map.has(parsed.data)) {
73:       throw new Error(
74:         "Priority branches must have unique named bands: Must have, Should have, Could have, Won't have. Use another mode for arbitrary labels.",
75:       );
76:     }
77:     map.set(parsed.data, index);
78:   }
79:   const bands = Priority.options;
80:   if (labels.length > 4 || bands.slice(0, labels.length).some((band) => !map.has(band))) {
81:     throw new Error(
82:       "Priority branches must include contiguous upper bands: Must + Should, optionally Could and Won't. Missing intermediate bands are ambiguous.",
83:     );
84:   }
85:   const lowest = bands[labels.length - 1]!;
86:   return (priority: Priority, id: string, log: BlockContext["log"]): number => {
87:     const matched = map.get(priority);
88:     if (matched !== undefined) return matched;
89:     const branch = map.get(lowest)!;
90:     log(
91:       `${id}: priority ${priority} has no named branch; fallback to ${labels[branch]} (out-${branch}), coarsening omitted lower bands.`,
92:     );
93:     return branch;
94:   };
95: }

97: export async function routePriority(
98:   items: PromptItem[],
99:   params: SplitterParams,
100:   ctx: BlockContext,
101: ): Promise<Map<string, number>> {
102:   const branchFor = priorityBranches(params.branches);
103:   const scoring = Settings.shape.scoring.parse(ctx.settings.scoring);
104:   const result = new Map<string, number>();
105:   const pending: PromptItem[] = [];
106:   ctx.log(
107:     "WS8 deterministic scorer is unavailable. Reuse existing priority/factor values; missing factors use provisional LLM judgement only for routing, without persisting requirement changes.",
108:   );
109:   for (const entry of items) {
110:     ctx.signal.throwIfAborted();
111:     const requirement = entry.layer === "requirements" ? (entry.item as Requirement) : undefined;
112:     if (requirement?.priority) {
113:       const branch = branchFor(requirement.priority, entry.id, ctx.log);
114:       result.set(entry.id, branch);
115:       ctx.log(
116:         `${entry.id}: existing priority ${requirement.priority} preserved (including any human override); routed to out-${branch}.`,
117:       );
118:     } else if (requirement?.score) {
119:       const values = Object.fromEntries(
120:         ScoreFactor.options.map((factor) => [factor, requirement.score!.factors[factor].value]),
121:       ) as Record<ScoreFactor, number>;
122:       const total = weightedTotal(values, scoring.weights);
123:       const priority = priorityForScore(total, scoring.thresholds);
124:       const branch = branchFor(priority, entry.id, ctx.log);
125:       result.set(entry.id, branch);
126:       ctx.log(
127:         `${entry.id}: reused existing factor values with current Settings weights/thresholds; total ${total}/100, priority ${priority}, out-${branch}. Stored score unchanged.`,
128:       );
129:       for (const factor of ScoreFactor.options)
130:         ctx.log(
131:           `${entry.id}: ${factor}=${values[factor]}/5, weight=${scoring.weights[factor]}; ${requirement.score.factors[factor].note}`,
132:         );
133:     } else pending.push(entry);
134:   }
135:   const payload = (batch: PromptItem[]) => ({
136:     contract: "reqflow.ai-splitter.scoring@1",
137:     mode: "priority",
138:     branches: params.branches,
139:     instruction: "",
140:     items: batch,
141:     scope: ctx.scope,
142:     factors: ScoreFactor.options,
143:   });
144:   const groups = batches(pending, payload);
145:   let completed = result.size;
146:   ctx.progress(
147:     completed / items.length,
148:     `Resolved ${completed}/${items.length} existing priorities`,
149:   );
150:   for (const [index, batch] of groups.entries()) {
151:     ctx.signal.throwIfAborted();
152:     ctx.log(
153:       `Provisional scoring batch ${index + 1}/${groups.length}: ${batch.length} primary items.`,
154:     );
155:     const { object, model } = await generate(ctx, {
156:       system: SCORING_SYSTEM,
157:       prompt: JSON.stringify(payload(batch)),
158:       schema: Scores,
159:       tier: params.model,
160:     });
161:     const scores = validateIds(
162:       object.scores,
163:       batch.map((item) => item.id),
164:     );
165:     for (const entry of batch) {
166:       const score = scores.get(entry.id)!;
167:       for (const factor of ScoreFactor.options) {
168:         validateNote(score.factors[factor].note, entry, factor);
169:       }
170:       const values = Object.fromEntries(
171:         ScoreFactor.options.map((factor) => [factor, score.factors[factor].value]),
172:       ) as Record<ScoreFactor, number>;
173:       const total = weightedTotal(values, scoring.weights);
174:       const priority = priorityForScore(total, scoring.thresholds);
175:       const branch = branchFor(priority, entry.id, ctx.log);
176:       result.set(entry.id, branch);
177:       ctx.log(
178:         `${entry.id}: provisional LLM factors (${model}), total ${total}/100, priority ${priority}, out-${branch}; judgement is not measured data or a human decision. Requirement unchanged.`,
179:       );
180:       for (const factor of ScoreFactor.options)
181:         ctx.log(
182:           `${entry.id}: ${factor}=${values[factor]}/5, weight=${scoring.weights[factor]}; ${score.factors[factor].note}`,
183:         );
184:     }
185:     completed += batch.length;
186:     ctx.progress(completed / items.length, `Scored ${completed}/${items.length} primary items`);
187:   }
188:   return result;
189: }

93: 
94: ## Prioritization logic (explainable by design)
95: 
96: Six factors, each scored 0–5 with a one-line justification. On every factor, higher means "more worth doing":
97: customer impact · evidence strength · competitive gap · trend momentum (3–5 yr) · brand fit ·
98: ease (the inverse of rough effort/cost).
99: 
100: `score = 100 × Σ(weight × value) / (5 × Σ weight)`. The score maps to **must / should / could / won't**
101: using the thresholds set in Settings. The PM can override the priority, and the override is audited.
102: Evidence level is shown **next to** the score, never hidden inside it. A high score built on
103: D-level (assumption) evidence should catch the eye.
104: 
105: ## Evidence levels
106: 
107: **A** — several independent sources including quantitative BMW data · **B** — several sources, mostly
108: qualitative · **C** — a single source or anecdotal · **D** — rests mainly on forward-looking assumptions.
109: 
110: ## Scope rules (from the briefing)
111: 
112: - **In scope:** customer-facing attributes such as features, equipment, comfort, space, usability,
113:   infotainment and digital services, design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging
114:   _as the customer experiences them_, and variants and packages.
115: - **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, technical and engineering specs, and
116:   pricing or business cases. An AI Filter removes these, and every exclusion is logged with a reason.
117: 
118: ## Demo scenario
119: 
120: **BMW 1 Series (F70) · EU · 5-year horizon**, because BMW's data is for the F70: customer feedback,
121: customer studies (the F70 next to the G60/G68 5 Series and G70 7 Series), sales volumes and the option
122: list. The requirements are for the F70's successor. This is the default scope in Settings.
123: 
124: 1. Open the default template, attach the BMW files to the Raw blocks, enable web research, and run.
125: 2. Watch the blocks fill up, then click the AI Filter to see findings with their evidence.
126: 3. The run pauses at the HIL block. On the Car tab, open a must-have and trace it down to a verbatim customer quote.
127: 4. Challenge one requirement. The AI answers. Edit one, approve one with a priority override, and reject one.
128: 5. Resume the run, which publishes and exports. The audit trail shows the full history of one requirement.
129: 6. Switch the scope to another series or market in Settings to show the workflow isn't a one-off.

1: # ReqFlow — product definition
2: 
3: > Working name. One page, the source of truth for **what** we build. **How** is in
4: > [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), **who builds what** in [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md).
5: 
6: ## Problem
7: 
8: Defining the next generation of a BMW vehicle means working out what customers will value 3–5 years
9: from now. Today product managers do this by hand: they read customer feedback, BMW equipment and
10: sales data, customer studies and competitor and market information, then turn it into requirements.
11: It is slow, inconsistent and hard to trace. Months later nobody can say why a requirement exists,
12: what evidence backs it, or who decided it.
13: 
14: ## Product in one sentence
15: 
16: A visual, n8n-style **data flow** built from **building blocks** turns raw customer and market data into
17: **evidence-linked, prioritized car requirements**. A product manager reviews, challenges and decides on
18: them on the **Car** page, and every step is recorded in an **audit trail**.
19: 
20: > Customer requirement = customer-relevant attribute of a car. (BMW briefing)
21: 
22: ## Users
23: 
24: - **Product Manager (primary).** Owns the requirement set for one vehicle line × market. Makes every decision.
25: - **Analyst / PM ops (secondary).** Builds and tunes workflows, connects data and adjusts scoring in Settings.
26: 
27: ## The app — three tabs
28: 
29: A **native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux**, not a web app. Everything runs locally on
30: the PM's machine. BMW files are imported through the system file dialog, results are exported
31: through the save dialog, and API keys are stored in the OS keychain. Only the AI and web-research
32: calls leave the machine. Layout (sketch: `context/Building_Blocks.jpeg`): the page fills the window, and
33: a tab bar at the bottom switches between **Data Flow · Car · Settings** (⌘/Ctrl + 1–3).
34: 
35: | Tab           | What the user does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
36: | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
37: | **Data Flow** | **Building Blocks** on the left, the **Workplace** on the right. Drag blocks (or click them) onto the workplace, connect an output to an input, and set each block's parameters in the inspector. Custom, Research and AI Filter blocks **expand** into their own inner workplace, built from the same blocks. Later: run the flow, see each block's status, counts and logs, and inspect what it produced. A run **pauses at HIL blocks** until a person has reviewed.                                                                                                            |
38: | **Car**       | The output: what the next car should offer. Today a placeholder (a car and the global vehicle/market). WS3 builds the requirement list here. Each requirement has an ID, title, description, measurable targets, category, score breakdown, priority with rationale, evidence level, assumptions, uncertainties, conflicting evidence and status, with a drill-down requirement → findings → verbatim evidence → source, **approve / reject / defer / edit / challenge** (rationale required) and the **audit trail**: who or what changed what, when, from what to what, and why. |
39: | **Settings**  | **App** (theme, workplace grid and minimap, delete confirmation) · **Global parameters** (vehicle line, derivative, code, market, horizon; prioritization weights and thresholds with a live example; output language) · **AI & research** (provider, models, temperature, web research, domains, API-key status) · **Collaboration** (your name and role for the audit trail, team members and invitations, sharing via a shared folder or Git repo, notifications, four-eyes approval) · **About**.                                                                              |
40: 
41: ## The building blocks
42: 
43: Each block is specified as **Block (params / inner workplace / inputs / outputs)**, e.g. HIL (t/f/1/1)
44: = has parameters, no inner workplace, 1 input, 1 output. "n" = one port per entry of a list parameter.
45: Blocks are finalized one at a time; **State** says how far each one is.
46: 
47: | Block           | Spec      | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | State                                                                                             |
48: | --------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
49: | **Custom**      | (f/t/1/1) | An empty block. Build any sub-flow inside it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | placeholder                                                                                       |
50: | **Raw**         | (t/f/0/1) | Brings in an Excel (.xlsx) or CSV file or a SQLite query as one unified data stream: one record per row (repeated feedback rows merged), report-style sheets read by section, plus usage findings from take rates and sales volumes. "Preview data" shows the parsed result right away.                                         | **built**: .xlsx, CSV, SQLite; reads BMW's exports; runs in a flow once the executor exists (WS1) |
51: | **Research**    | (t/t/0/1) | Searches the web; emits a data stream in the same format as Raw.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | placeholder params                                                                                |
52: | **AI Filter**   | (t/t/1/1) | Keeps the items that match a criterion written in plain language.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | placeholder params                                                                                |
53: | **AI Splitter** | (t/f/1/n) | Sorts every item into one branch (e.g. by priority or category). One output per branch.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | placeholder params                                                                                |
54: | **HIL**         | (t/f/1/1) | Human in the loop (capacitor icon). The flow waits here until a person has reviewed what arrived, then passes it on. **Double-click opens the review report:** a flow chart of how the data was collected (every step it passed through, across inner workplaces) and a table icon on every step to see the data at that point. | **finalized** — report and pause/continue logic built; runs once the executor exists (WS1)        |
55: | **Add to Car**  | (t/f/n/0) | Adds what arrives to the car's requirements. The input it arrives on sets the ranking.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | placeholder params                                                                                |
56: 
57: Spec and ports: `packages/core/src/blocks.ts`. Implementations: `packages/blocks/src/<block>/`.
58: 
59: ## Default flow (template)
60: 
61: The default template mirrors the BMW process slide (`context/` image). The robot icon means the AI does the step on its own; the person icon means a human is involved.
62: 
63: ```
64: Situation analysis        Structure & context          Prioritization                  Review          Documentation
65: ──────────────────        ───────────────────          ──────────────                  ──────          ─────────────
66: Raw: customer feedback ┐
67: Raw: customer study    ┤
68: Raw: equipment data    ┼─▶ AI Filter ───────────────▶ AI Splitter ──must───▶ 🧑 HIL ──┐
69: Raw: sales volumes     ┤   "customer-facing only"     "by priority" ──should─▶ 🧑 HIL ──┼─▶ Add to Car
70: Research: web          ┘   (findings + evidence;       (explainable ──could─────────────┘   (requirements,
71:                             drops regulatory,           weighted       (unreviewed)          ranked by input)
72:                             engineering, pricing)       score)
73: ```
74: 
75: **Where AI acts on its own:** ingestion (Raw, Research), filtering and extracting evidence-linked
76: findings (AI Filter), scoring and routing (AI Splitter), drafting requirements (Add to Car).
77: **Where a human must act:** at every HIL block, and when approving, rejecting, deferring or editing a
78: requirement, overriding a priority or answering a challenge on the Car tab. The AI can **never** set
79: a requirement to `approved` or `rejected`.

59: /**
60:  * Dependency closure. Supporting context may occur on several branches; primary items never do.
61:  * For requirements, themes connected to cited findings are contextual clusters, including siblings.
62:  * Missing referenced entities remain missing and are reported, never fabricated or removed from IDs.
63:  */
64: export function evidenceIndex(input: PipelineData, log: (message: string) => void) {
65:   const primary = primaryLayer(input);
66:   const maps = {
67:     sources: new Map(input.sources.map((v) => [v.id, v])),
68:     records: new Map(input.records.map((v) => [v.id, v])),
69:     findings: new Map(input.findings.map((v) => [v.id, v])),
70:     themes: new Map(input.themes.map((v) => [v.id, v])),
71:     requirements: new Map(input.requirements.map((v) => [v.id, v])),
72:   };
73:   const positions = new Map(
74:     DATA_KEYS.flatMap((key) => input[key].map((item, index) => [item.id, index] as const)),
75:   );
76:   function selected<T extends { id: string }>(map: Map<string, T>, ids: Set<string>): T[] {
77:     return [...ids]
78:       .map((id) => map.get(id)!)
79:       .sort((a, b) => positions.get(a.id)! - positions.get(b.id)!);
80:   }
81:   const themesByFinding = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
82:   const findingsByTheme = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
83:   for (const theme of input.themes) {
84:     for (const findingId of theme.findingIds) {
85:       const ids = themesByFinding.get(findingId) ?? new Set<string>();
86:       ids.add(theme.id);
87:       themesByFinding.set(findingId, ids);
88:     }
89:   }
90:   for (const finding of input.findings) {
91:     if (!finding.themeId) continue;
92:     const ids = findingsByTheme.get(finding.themeId) ?? new Set<string>();
93:     ids.add(finding.id);
94:     findingsByTheme.set(finding.themeId, ids);
95:   }
96:   const warned = new Set<string>();
97:   function missing(key: DataKey, id: string) {
98:     const ref = `${key}:${id}`;
99:     if (!warned.has(ref))
100:       log(`Unavailable referenced ${key} ${id}; retaining original link, no evidence invented.`);
101:     warned.add(ref);
102:   }
103:   return {
104:     /** Build small prompt contexts from indexes, not one full input scan per primary item. */
105:     context(membership: Membership): PipelineData {
106:       return {
107:         ...input,
108:         sources: selected(maps.sources, membership.sources),
109:         records: selected(maps.records, membership.records),
110:         findings: selected(maps.findings, membership.findings),
111:         themes: selected(maps.themes, membership.themes),
112:         requirements: selected(maps.requirements, membership.requirements),
113:       };
114:     },
115:     closure(layer: DataKey, id: string): Membership {
116:       const membership = emptyMembership();
117:       function add(key: DataKey, ref: string): void {
118:         if (membership[key].has(ref)) return;
119:         if (!maps[key].has(ref)) {
120:           missing(key, ref);
121:           return;
122:         }
123:         membership[key].add(ref);
124:         switch (key) {
125:           case "requirements": {
126:             const requirement = maps.requirements.get(ref)!;
127:             const findingIds = [...requirement.findingIds, ...requirement.conflictingFindingIds];
128:             for (const findingId of findingIds) {
129:               add("findings", findingId);
130:               for (const themeId of themesByFinding.get(findingId) ?? []) add("themes", themeId);
131:               const themeId = maps.findings.get(findingId)?.themeId;
132:               if (themeId) add("themes", themeId);
133:             }
134:             for (const sourceId of requirement.sourceIds) add("sources", sourceId);
135:             break;
136:           }
137:           case "themes": {
138:             for (const findingId of maps.themes.get(ref)!.findingIds) add("findings", findingId);
139:             for (const findingId of findingsByTheme.get(ref) ?? []) add("findings", findingId);
140:             break;
141:           }
142:           case "findings": {
143:             const finding = maps.findings.get(ref)!;
144:             // Supporting themes may be shared; classified primary themes must not be duplicated.
145:             if (finding.themeId && primary !== "themes") add("themes", finding.themeId);
146:             for (const evidence of finding.evidence) {
147:               add("sources", evidence.sourceId);
148:               if (evidence.recordId) add("records", evidence.recordId);
149:             }
150:             break;
151:           }
152:           case "records":
153:             add("sources", maps.records.get(ref)!.sourceId);
154:             break;
155:           case "sources":
156:             break;
157:         }
158:       }
159:       add(layer, id);
160:       return membership;
161:     },
162:   };
163: }

165: /** Orphans are unclassified context, retained once on the first occupied branch (lowest output index). */
166: export function retainOrphans(
167:   input: PipelineData,
168:   memberships: Membership[],
169:   index: ReturnType<typeof evidenceIndex>,
170:   log: (message: string) => void,
171: ): void {
172:   const first = memberships.find((membership) => DATA_KEYS.some((key) => membership[key].size));
173:   if (!first) return;
174:   const counts: string[] = [];
175:   for (const key of DATA_KEYS) {
176:     const referenced = new Set(memberships.flatMap((membership) => [...membership[key]]));
177:     const orphans = input[key].filter((item) => !referenced.has(item.id));
178:     for (const item of orphans) {
179:       const closure = index.closure(key, item.id);
180:       for (const dependencyKey of DATA_KEYS) {
181:         for (const id of closure[dependencyKey]) first[dependencyKey].add(id);
182:       }
183:     }
184:     if (orphans.length) counts.push(`${orphans.length} ${key}`);
185:   }
186:   if (counts.length)
187:     log(
188:       `Retained orphan upstream context (${counts.join(", ")}) once on out-${memberships.indexOf(first)} with dependency closure; evidence may be shared, not independently classified.`,
189:     );
190: }
191: 
192: export function emptyOutputs(count: number): Record<string, PipelineData> {
193:   return Object.fromEntries(
194:     Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) => [`out-${i}`, emptyPipelineData()]),
195:   );
196: }

40: /**
41:  * Transport only the documented Anthropic subset. Original Zod validation remains authoritative.
42:  * Unsupported scalar/array constraints become descriptions, matching SDK transformation behavior.
43:  * https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs#json-schema-limitations
44:  */
45: export function anthropicSchema(original: JsonSchema): JsonSchema {
46:   const output: JsonSchema = {};
47:   const constraints: string[] = [];
48:   for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(original)) {
49:     if (key === "$schema") continue;
50:     if (
51:       LOCAL_CONSTRAINTS.has(key) ||
52:       (key === "minItems" && value !== 0 && value !== 1) ||
53:       (key === "format" && !FORMATS.has(value as string))
54:     ) {
55:       constraints.push(`${key}: ${JSON.stringify(value)}`);
56:     } else if (ANNOTATIONS.has(key) || key === "format" || key === "minItems") {
57:       if (
58:         key === "enum" &&
59:         (value as unknown[]).some(
60:           (item) => item !== null && !["string", "number", "boolean"].includes(typeof item),
61:         )
62:       ) {
63:         throw new Error("Anthropic structured outputs do not support complex enum values");
64:       }
65:       output[key] = value;
66:     } else if (key === "properties" || key === "$defs" || key === "definitions") {
67:       output[key] = Object.fromEntries(
68:         Object.entries(value as Record<string, JsonSchema>).map(([name, schema]) => [
69:           name,
70:           anthropicSchema(schema),
71:         ]),
72:       );
73:     } else if (key === "items") {
74:       output.items = anthropicSchema(value as JsonSchema);
75:     } else if (key === "anyOf" || key === "allOf") {
76:       const alternatives = value as JsonSchema[];
77:       if (key === "allOf" && alternatives.some((schema) => "$ref" in schema)) {
78:         throw new Error("Anthropic structured outputs do not support allOf with $ref");
79:       }
80:       output[key] = alternatives.map(anthropicSchema);
81:     } else if (key === "$ref") {
82:       if (typeof value !== "string" || !value.startsWith("#/")) {
83:         throw new Error("Anthropic structured outputs do not support external references");
84:       }
85:       output.$ref = value;
86:     } else if (key === "additionalProperties") {
87:       if (typeof value === "object") {
88:         throw new Error(
89:           "Anthropic structured outputs require explicit object properties; schema-valued additionalProperties is unsupported",
90:         );
91:       }
92:       output.additionalProperties = false;
93:     } else {
94:       throw new Error(`Unsupported Anthropic schema keyword ${key}`);
95:     }
96:   }
97:   if (
98:     output.type === "object" ||
99:     output.properties ||
100:     (Array.isArray(output.type) && output.type.includes("object"))
101:   ) {
102:     output.additionalProperties = false;
103:   }
104:   if (constraints.length) {
105:     output.description = [
106:       output.description,
107:       `Local validation constraints: {${constraints.join(", ")}}.`,
108:     ]
109:       .filter(Boolean)
110:       .join(" ");
111:   }
112:   return output;
113: }

# AGENTS.md — read this first

## What we're building

**ReqFlow** is a hackathon prototype for the BMW challenge _"AI for Product Decision Making"_: a
**native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron, not a web app) with three tabs. On
**Data Flow**, an n8n-style flow of **building blocks** (Custom, Raw, Research, AI Filter, AI Splitter,
HIL, Add to Car; some expand into their own inner workplace) turns customer and market data into
prioritized, evidence-linked car requirements. The **Car** tab shows them for the PM to review, and
**Settings** configures the app, global parameters and collaboration. Full spec: [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md). Your task: [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md).
Current state and handoffs: [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).

## The challenge in brief (from `context/`)

- **Goal:** help BMW product managers define, justify and prioritize **customer-facing requirements
  for the successor** of an existing vehicle, thinking **3–5 years ahead**. The PM stays in control of
  every decision.
- **Vehicles and markets:** the 1, 5 or 7 Series, in Europe, China or the US. Demo **one derivative in one
  market** (ours: 1 Series F70, EU), but don't build a one-off.
- **BMW provides, per vehicle:** customer feedback, equipment data, sales volumes and a customer study.
  We may add web sources such as competitors, reviews and market or technology trends.
- **The app must:** ingest the data and enrich it from the web → extract signals (complaints, unmet needs,
  competitor advantages, trends), **each linked to its sources** → derive clear, actionable, realistic
  requirements → prioritize them with explainable logic → let the PM approve, reject, edit or challenge
  them → record everything in an **audit trail** (who or what, when, and why).
- **Each requirement needs:** a unique ID, an actionable description, linked findings and sources, a
  priority or score, the prioritization rationale, an evidence level, assumptions and uncertainties, and
  a decision status.
- **In scope:** features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment and digital services,
  design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging as the customer experiences them,
  and variants and packages. **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, engineering specs, and
  pricing or business cases (rough effort may be used as a priority factor).
- **Judges value:** trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning, thoughtful prioritization, honest
  handling of uncertainty and **conflicting evidence**, and focus on customer value. Depth in one area
  beats shallow coverage of everything.
- **BMW process we mirror:** situation analysis → structure and context (classify, cluster, dedupe) →
  requirements definition (measurable targets and acceptance criteria) → prioritization (customer and
  business) → documentation and tracking. _"From 1 billion findings to 1,000 requirements to one car."_

## Rules for every agent

1. **Stay in your lane.** Edit only the paths your workstream owns (see WORKSTREAMS.md). Do you need
   something changed elsewhere? Write it in your final report instead of editing it yourself.
2. **`packages/core` is the contract.** Build against it and don't change it on your own. If you need a
   contract change, propose it in your final report. The lead merges contract changes.
3. **No real data in git, logs or transcripts.** BMW files go in `data/raw/` (gitignored). Entire
   publishes session transcripts, so when you inspect them, print only structure and counts (sheet
   and column names, row counts), never cell values, and never send them to delegated agents.
   Committed tests use synthetic data (`@reqflow/core/fixtures`, `data/samples/`). Never commit or
   print API keys.
4. **No silent failures.** Validate inputs with the Zod schemas, throw clear errors, and never invent
   sources or evidence. Every finding needs a verbatim excerpt.
5. **AI never decides.** Only a human sets `approved`, `rejected` or `deferred`. Every change to a
   requirement writes an AuditEvent.

Replaced the existing **AI Splitter** and merged it into `main`: [PR #7](https://github.com/EHL-Team-Eichel/reqflow/pull/7).

It now supports:
- **1 input, 2–10 outputs**
- Parameters and a double-click **inner workspace**
- Priority, category, sentiment and custom routing
- Exactly-once routing of primary items, with linked evidence preserved
- Existing workflows using the replacement automatically

**Verified:** 204 tests passed, 24 skipped; typecheck, formatting and desktop smoke passed with 29 screenshots.

Missing priority factors remain explicitly provisional until WS8 scoring is ready. Anthropic transport was tested offline with mocked HTTP.
did u push?

Yes—pushed `ws7-ai-splitter` and merged [PR #7](https://github.com/EHL-Team-Eichel/reqflow/pull/7) into **`main`**.

Merge commit: `9dccb5a`.
what does the splitter do?

The **AI Splitter sorts incoming data into named branches**: **1 input → 2–10 outputs**.

### How it splits
You choose a mode in its parameters:
- **Priority:** Must / Should / Could / Won’t
- **Category:** groups such as Comfort, Infotainment or Charging
- **Sentiment:** groups such as Positive, Negative or Mixed
- **Custom:** follows your instruction and branch names

For example, customer findings could be split into **Comfort**, **Infotainment** and **Charging**, with each branch connected to a different downstream block.

### What happens to the data
- It routes the most developed data available: **requirements → themes → findings → raw records**.
- Each primary item goes to **exactly one output**.
- Related sources and evidence travel with it; shared evidence can accompany several branches.
- Logs explain assignments and assumptions.
- Human priorities and approval statuses are preserved.

### Double-click
Opens its **inner workspace**. The default boundary-only workspace uses built-in routing. Adding blocks or connections makes your sub-flow control the routing.

**Current caveats:** Mock mode provides deterministic demo results; Anthropic mode uses the configured AI model. Priority judgements without existing factor scores are explicitly provisional until WS8 scoring is integrated.
what exactly are branch names

**Branch names are the labels you give each output—and the groups the splitter sorts items into.**

For example, with category splitting:

| Branch name | Output receives |
|---|---|
| Comfort | Items about seats, noise or ride comfort |
| Infotainment | Items about screens, navigation or controls |
| Charging | Items about charging and range |

You set these in the splitter’s **Branches** parameter. Each name creates one output connector, in list order.

- **Category, sentiment or custom mode:** choose meaningful names yourself. The AI uses them as the available groups.
- **Priority mode:** use **Must have**, **Should have**, optionally **Could have** and **Won’t have**.

The names describe **where data belongs**; connecting those outputs determines **where it goes next**.

# AGENTS.md — read this first

## What we're building

**ReqFlow** is a hackathon prototype for the BMW challenge _"AI for Product Decision Making"_: a
**native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron, not a web app) with three tabs. On
**Data Flow**, an n8n-style flow of **building blocks** (Custom, Raw, Research, AI Filter, AI Splitter,
HIL, Add to Car; some expand into their own inner workplace) turns customer and market data into
prioritized, evidence-linked car requirements. The **Car** tab shows them for the PM to review, and
**Settings** configures the app, global parameters and collaboration. Full spec: [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md). Your task: [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md).
Current state and handoffs: [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).

## The challenge in brief (from `context/`)

- **Goal:** help BMW product managers define, justify and prioritize **customer-facing requirements
  for the successor** of an existing vehicle, thinking **3–5 years ahead**. The PM stays in control of
  every decision.
- **Vehicles and markets:** the 1, 5 or 7 Series, in Europe, China or the US. Demo **one derivative in one
  market** (ours: 1 Series F70, EU), but don't build a one-off.
- **BMW provides, per vehicle:** customer feedback, equipment data, sales volumes and a customer study.
  We may add web sources such as competitors, reviews and market or technology trends.
- **The app must:** ingest the data and enrich it from the web → extract signals (complaints, unmet needs,
  competitor advantages, trends), **each linked to its sources** → derive clear, actionable, realistic
  requirements → prioritize them with explainable logic → let the PM approve, reject, edit or challenge
  them → record everything in an **audit trail** (who or what, when, and why).
- **Each requirement needs:** a unique ID, an actionable description, linked findings and sources, a
  priority or score, the prioritization rationale, an evidence level, assumptions and uncertainties, and
  a decision status.
- **In scope:** features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment and digital services,
  design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging as the customer experiences them,
  and variants and packages. **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, engineering specs, and
  pricing or business cases (rough effort may be used as a priority factor).
- **Judges value:** trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning, thoughtful prioritization, honest
  handling of uncertainty and **conflicting evidence**, and focus on customer value. Depth in one area
  beats shallow coverage of everything.
- **BMW process we mirror:** situation analysis → structure and context (classify, cluster, dedupe) →
  requirements definition (measurable targets and acceptance criteria) → prioritization (customer and
  business) → documentation and tracking. _"From 1 billion findings to 1,000 requirements to one car."_

## Rules for every agent

1. **Stay in your lane.** Edit only the paths your workstream owns (see WORKSTREAMS.md). Do you need
   something changed elsewhere? Write it in your final report instead of editing it yourself.
2. **`packages/core` is the contract.** Build against it and don't change it on your own. If you need a
   contract change, propose it in your final report. The lead merges contract changes.
3. **No real data in git, logs or transcripts.** BMW files go in `data/raw/` (gitignored). Entire
   publishes session transcripts, so when you inspect them, print only structure and counts (sheet
   and column names, row counts), never cell values, and never send them to delegated agents.
   Committed tests use synthetic data (`@reqflow/core/fixtures`, `data/samples/`). Never commit or
   print API keys.
4. **No silent failures.** Validate inputs with the Zod schemas, throw clear errors, and never invent
   sources or evidence. Every finding needs a verbatim excerpt.
5. **AI never decides.** Only a human sets `approved`, `rejected` or `deferred`. Every change to a
   requirement writes an AuditEvent.
6. **Prove it works.** Add colocated `*.test.ts` files. Before you report done, run
   `npm run typecheck && npm test` from the repo root. For UI work, also run `npm run smoke` and look at
   the screenshots in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`.
7. **Respect the process split.** UI code (renderer) has no Node, no `fs` and no network. It talks to the
   main process only through `api` from `@/lib/api` (contract: `packages/core/src/ipc.ts`). Data, AI
   calls, files and API keys live in the main process. Build paths with `node:path` so they work on Windows.
8. **Sessions are tracked with [Entire](https://github.com/entireio/cli).** Commit with plain `git`.
   Entire attaches your session to each commit as a checkpoint and pushes it on `git push`. Don't
   remove its hooks (`.claude/settings.json`, `.git/hooks`) and never put secrets in prompts.

9. **Hand off in [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).** Claim your workstream there when you start; your
   tasks are the checklist in its section, in priority order. Update your own section (and only that
   one) when you finish a slice, get blocked or stop: tick done tasks, add a log entry. The next agent
   starts from it. The repo and Entire transcripts are **public**, so never paste keys or BMW data anywhere.

## Commands (repo root, Node ≥ 22.13; works on Windows, macOS, Linux)

```
npm install          # once
npm run dev          # opens the desktop app with hot reload
npm run smoke        # builds, screenshots every screen, checks the IPC bridge
npm test             # vitest, all packages
npm run typecheck    # all workspaces
npm run format       # prettier
npm run package      # installer for your OS → apps/desktop/release/
```

2: import { Finding, Theme } from "./finding";
